{"units":[
{"unit":"u1","blocks":[],"dropped_reason":"Fictional-demonstration disclaimer; boilerplate notice, not evidence content."},
{"unit":"u2","blocks":[{"text":"VELMARA (velmaratinib) — PAYER AND HTA STAKEHOLDER INTERVIEWS","kind":"title","heading":null}],"dropped_reason":null},
{"unit":"u3","blocks":[{"text":"Second-line EGFR-mutant non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC)","kind":"title","heading":null}],"dropped_reason":null},
{"unit":"u4","blocks":[{"text":"Interview programme summary and selected transcript excerpts","kind":"title","heading":null}],"dropped_reason":null},
{"unit":"u5","blocks":[{"text":"Prepared by: Global HEOR, with Market Access Insights","kind":"paragraph","heading":null}],"dropped_reason":null},
{"unit":"u6","blocks":[{"text":"Fieldwork: June to August 2026","kind":"paragraph","heading":null}],"dropped_reason":null},
{"unit":"u7","blocks":[{"text":"Status: Internal, for evidence planning only","kind":"paragraph","heading":null}],"dropped_reason":null},
{"unit":"u8","blocks":[{"text":"1. PURPOSE AND METHOD","kind":"heading","heading":null}],"dropped_reason":null},
{"unit":"u9","blocks":[{"text":"This programme was commissioned to understand what US national payers, integrated delivery network (IDN) pathway committees and EU5 health technology assessment (HTA) advisers will need to see before the planned US payer P&T reviews and EU5 HTA submissions, which are expected to conclude by 31 March 2027.","kind":"paragraph","heading":"1. PURPOSE AND METHOD"}],"dropped_reason":null},
{"unit":"u10","blocks":[{"text":"We completed twelve 60-minute, double-blinded telephone interviews using a semi-structured discussion guide. Respondents were recruited through an independent fieldwork agency and paid fair-market-value honoraria. All quotations below are anonymised and lightly edited for readability.","kind":"paragraph","heading":"1. PURPOSE AND METHOD"}],"dropped_reason":null},
{"unit":"u11","blocks":[{"text":"Respondent mix:","kind":"paragraph","heading":"1. PURPOSE AND METHOD"}],"dropped_reason":null},
{"unit":"u12","blocks":[{"text":"- R1 to R4: US national and regional payers (pharmacy directors and medical directors, commercial and Medicare Advantage).","kind":"bullet","heading":"1. PURPOSE AND METHOD"}],"dropped_reason":null},
{"unit":"u13","blocks":[{"text":"- R5 and R6: US IDN oncology pathway leads.","kind":"bullet","heading":"1. PURPOSE AND METHOD"}],"dropped_reason":null},
{"unit":"u14","blocks":[{"text":"- R7 to R10: EU5 HTA advisers and former HTA committee members (two in Germany, one in France, one in England).","kind":"bullet","heading":"1. PURPOSE AND METHOD"}],"dropped_reason":null},
{"unit":"u15","blocks":[{"text":"- R11 and R12: health economists who regularly build cost-effectiveness and budget-impact models for oncology submissions.","kind":"bullet","heading":"1. PURPOSE AND METHOD"}],"dropped_reason":null},
{"unit":"u16","blocks":[{"text":"Stimulus: respondents saw a one-page product profile (VEL-301 Phase III design versus osimertinib, expected primary PFS readout, CNS sub-study, safety monitoring plan) and a draft value story. They did not see any unpublished data.","kind":"paragraph","heading":"1. PURPOSE AND METHOD"}],"dropped_reason":null},
{"unit":"u17","blocks":[{"text":"2. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY","kind":"heading","heading":null}],"dropped_reason":null},
{"unit":"u18","blocks":[{"text":"Across the twelve interviews, five themes recurred. They are ordered by how often respondents raised them without prompting.","kind":"paragraph","heading":"2. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY"}],"dropped_reason":null},
{"unit":"u19","blocks":[{"text":"Theme A. The economic burden of recurrence is poorly characterised. Every payer and both health economists said that the model will hinge on what happens after progression on velmaratinib: repeat imaging and biopsies, subsequent lines of therapy, hospitalisations and emergency department visits. Nobody could point to good routine-practice data on the direct costs of repeat procedures in this population.","kind":"paragraph","heading":"2. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY"}],"dropped_reason":null},
{"unit":"u20","blocks":[{"text":"Theme B. Comparative effectiveness in elderly patients is the most likely HTA sticking point. All four EU5 advisers expect an HTA committee to ask how Velmara performs against the regional standard of care in patients aged 65 and over, and specifically in frail patients. The single-arm chart review currently running in two EU5 centres was seen as helpful context but \"not an answer to the comparative question\".","kind":"paragraph","heading":"2. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY"}],"dropped_reason":null},
{"unit":"u21","blocks":[{"text":"Theme C. US payers will look hard at persistence and real-world duration of therapy. Three of four US payers said six-month discontinuation and persistence in routine care is a standard question at P&T for oral oncolytics and that trial persistence is not trusted.","kind":"paragraph","heading":"2. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY"}],"dropped_reason":null},
{"unit":"u22","blocks":[{"text":"Theme D. Budget impact under the Inflation Reduction Act (IRA) negotiated-price scenarios is now a routine request. Payers want to see budget impact under plausible IRA net-price scenarios for the class, not only at list price.","kind":"paragraph","heading":"2. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY"}],"dropped_reason":null},
{"unit":"u23","blocks":[{"text":"Theme E. Treatment sequencing after osimertinib is unclear to payers and pathway committees. IDN leads want to understand where Velmara sits relative to NX-441 and platinum-based chemotherapy after osimertinib failure, and whether real-world sequencing data exist.","kind":"paragraph","heading":"2. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY"}],"dropped_reason":null},
{"unit":"u24","blocks":[{"text":"Lower-frequency themes: caregiver burden and patient-reported outcomes in frail patients (raised by two EU5 advisers); intracranial efficacy as a driver of value for patients with brain metastases (raised by both IDN leads); long-term overall survival maturity (raised by all HTA advisers, but as an expected limitation rather than a blocker).","kind":"paragraph","heading":"2. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY"}],"dropped_reason":null},
{"unit":"u25","blocks":[{"text":"3. THEME A — ECONOMIC BURDEN OF RECURRENCE","kind":"heading","heading":null}],"dropped_reason":null},
{"unit":"u26","blocks":[{"text":"R11 (health economist): \"When I build the model for a second-line EGFR agent, the post-progression health state is where I have the least to go on. I have trial-based utilities, but I do not have good costs for what actually happens after recurrence in routine practice: the repeat CT and MRI, the second biopsy or liquid biopsy, the radiotherapy for new brain lesions, and the next line of treatment. Right now I would be using assumptions from older chemotherapy-era studies, and a committee will see straight through that.\"","kind":"paragraph","heading":"3. THEME A — ECONOMIC BURDEN OF RECURRENCE"}],"dropped_reason":null},
{"unit":"u27","blocks":[{"text":"R12 (health economist): \"The burden of recurrence is the single biggest driver of incremental cost in my experience. If you can give me real-world data on the cost of recurrence after a third-generation TKI, broken down by procedure, you remove my largest source of uncertainty.\"","kind":"paragraph","heading":"3. THEME A — ECONOMIC BURDEN OF RECURRENCE"}],"dropped_reason":null},
{"unit":"u28","blocks":[{"text":"R2 (US national payer, medical director): \"We see a lot of downstream utilisation after progression: admissions, ED visits for symptom control, and imaging. We do not have that broken out for this population. If the manufacturer can show it, it helps the conversation.\"","kind":"paragraph","heading":"3. THEME A — ECONOMIC BURDEN OF RECURRENCE"}],"dropped_reason":null},
{"unit":"u29","blocks":[{"text":"Interviewer note: when probed, no respondent was aware of a published routine-practice study of healthcare resource utilisation (HCRU) after EGFR TKI recurrence that separates hospitalisations, ED use and outpatient burden. Two mentioned small single-centre audits that they considered not generalisable.","kind":"paragraph","heading":"3. THEME A — ECONOMIC BURDEN OF RECURRENCE"}],"dropped_reason":null},
{"unit":"u30","blocks":[{"text":"4. THEME B — ELDERLY AND FRAIL PATIENTS","kind":"heading","heading":null}],"dropped_reason":null},
{"unit":"u31","blocks":[{"text":"R7 (German HTA adviser): \"The committee will ask about patients over 65. The trial population is younger than the patients we see. If the elderly subgroup in VEL-301 is small and not powered, it will be described as exploratory. That is fine, but then you need something else that compares Velmara with what we actually give these patients, which in many centres is still platinum doublet chemotherapy or best supportive care for the frail.\"","kind":"paragraph","heading":"4. THEME B — ELDERLY AND FRAIL PATIENTS"}],"dropped_reason":null},
{"unit":"u32","blocks":[{"text":"R8 (German HTA adviser): \"A single-arm chart review in elderly patients tells me what happened to patients on your drug. It does not tell me what would have happened on the comparator. For the benefit assessment I need a comparison, even an indirect one, done properly.\"","kind":"paragraph","heading":"4. THEME B — ELDERLY AND FRAIL PATIENTS"}],"dropped_reason":null},
{"unit":"u33","blocks":[{"text":"R9 (French HTA adviser): \"In France the question will be the place in therapy for the older patient. Please do not present the elderly subgroup of the pivotal trial as if it answers the question against regional standard of care. It does not, and the committee will say so.\"","kind":"paragraph","heading":"4. THEME B — ELDERLY AND FRAIL PATIENTS"}],"dropped_reason":null},
{"unit":"u34","blocks":[{"text":"R10 (English HTA adviser): \"Frailty matters as much as age. If you have anything on quality of life and patient-reported outcomes in frail patients, or on caregiver burden, it strengthens the case. At the moment that evidence is essentially absent for this class.\"","kind":"paragraph","heading":"4. THEME B — ELDERLY AND FRAIL PATIENTS"}],"dropped_reason":null},
{"unit":"u35","blocks":[{"text":"Interviewer note: all four EU5 advisers distinguished between (a) the VEL-301 elderly subgroup, which they regarded as descriptive, and (b) a powered or properly adjusted comparison of Velmara against regional standard of care in elderly patients, which none of them believed currently exists.","kind":"paragraph","heading":"4. THEME B — ELDERLY AND FRAIL PATIENTS"}],"dropped_reason":null},
{"unit":"u36","blocks":[{"text":"5. THEME C — PERSISTENCE AND DURATION OF THERAPY","kind":"heading","heading":null}],"dropped_reason":null},
{"unit":"u37","blocks":[{"text":"R1 (US regional payer, pharmacy director): \"For any oral oncolytic we ask about six-month persistence. Trials keep patients on drug in a way routine practice does not. Give me claims-based persistence and discontinuation, and the reasons if you can get them.\"","kind":"paragraph","heading":"5. THEME C — PERSISTENCE AND DURATION OF THERAPY"}],"dropped_reason":null},
{"unit":"u38","blocks":[{"text":"R3 (US national payer, Medicare Advantage): \"Discontinuation for toxicity drives waste. If there is an ILD or QT signal that leads to stopping, I want to know how often it happens outside academic centres.\"","kind":"paragraph","heading":"5. THEME C — PERSISTENCE AND DURATION OF THERAPY"}],"dropped_reason":null},
{"unit":"u39","blocks":[{"text":"R4 (US national payer, commercial): \"We will review this at P&T within about six months of launch. If you have early real-world persistence by then, it matters. If you do not, we will default to a step edit behind osimertinib progression and NX-441.\"","kind":"paragraph","heading":"5. THEME C — PERSISTENCE AND DURATION OF THERAPY"}],"dropped_reason":null},
{"unit":"u40","blocks":[{"text":"6. THEME D — BUDGET IMPACT UNDER IRA","kind":"heading","heading":null}],"dropped_reason":null},
{"unit":"u41","blocks":[{"text":"R2: \"Every oncology budget-impact model we see now needs IRA net-price scenarios for the class. Show us the budget impact at list price and under two or three plausible negotiated-price scenarios. We know nobody has the final numbers.\"","kind":"paragraph","heading":"6. THEME D — BUDGET IMPACT UNDER IRA"}],"dropped_reason":null},
{"unit":"u42","blocks":[{"text":"R12: \"I would build the budget-impact model with IRA scenarios as a structural feature rather than a sensitivity analysis. Payers will ask, and it is easier to have it built in.\"","kind":"paragraph","heading":"6. THEME D — BUDGET IMPACT UNDER IRA"}],"dropped_reason":null},
{"unit":"u43","blocks":[{"text":"7. THEME E — SEQUENCING AFTER OSIMERTINIB","kind":"heading","heading":null}],"dropped_reason":null},
{"unit":"u44","blocks":[{"text":"R5 (IDN pathway lead): \"Our pathway committee needs to place Velmara after osimertinib failure. The question is: before or after NX-441, and what about patients who go to chemotherapy first? We have no real-world sequencing data for this space, and the trials do not answer it.\"","kind":"paragraph","heading":"7. THEME E — SEQUENCING AFTER OSIMERTINIB"}],"dropped_reason":null},
{"unit":"u45","blocks":[{"text":"R6 (IDN pathway lead): \"For patients with brain metastases the intracranial response and how long it lasts would change our pathway. If the CNS data are strong, that becomes the differentiator for us.\"","kind":"paragraph","heading":"7. THEME E — SEQUENCING AFTER OSIMERTINIB"}],"dropped_reason":null},
{"unit":"u46","blocks":[{"text":"8. IMPLICATIONS FOR THE EVIDENCE PLAN (PROGRAMME TEAM VIEW)","kind":"heading","heading":null}],"dropped_reason":null},
{"unit":"u47","blocks":[{"text":"The programme team's synthesis, for discussion at the evidence-planning workshop:","kind":"paragraph","heading":"8. IMPLICATIONS FOR THE EVIDENCE PLAN (PROGRAMME TEAM VIEW)"}],"dropped_reason":null},
{"unit":"u48","blocks":[{"text":"- Highest priority: generate routine-practice evidence on the economic and clinical burden of recurrence (procedure-level direct costs, HCRU including hospitalisations and ED use), to feed the cost-effectiveness model against osimertinib before the CEA and budget-impact input freeze on 30 November 2026.","kind":"bullet","heading":"8. IMPLICATIONS FOR THE EVIDENCE PLAN (PROGRAMME TEAM VIEW)"}],"dropped_reason":null},
{"unit":"u49","blocks":[{"text":"- Highest priority: design a comparative-effectiveness approach for elderly patients against regional standard of care, distinct from the VEL-301 elderly subgroup and from the existing single-arm chart review, in time for the HTA elderly subgroup package due 15 January 2027.","kind":"bullet","heading":"8. IMPLICATIONS FOR THE EVIDENCE PLAN (PROGRAMME TEAM VIEW)"}],"dropped_reason":null},
{"unit":"u50","blocks":[{"text":"- High priority: a US claims-based persistence and six-month discontinuation study, ideally with early read-outs available for P&T.","kind":"bullet","heading":"8. IMPLICATIONS FOR THE EVIDENCE PLAN (PROGRAMME TEAM VIEW)"}],"dropped_reason":null},
{"unit":"u51","blocks":[{"text":"- Medium priority: build IRA negotiated-price scenarios into the budget-impact model.","kind":"bullet","heading":"8. IMPLICATIONS FOR THE EVIDENCE PLAN (PROGRAMME TEAM VIEW)"}],"dropped_reason":null},
{"unit":"u52","blocks":[{"text":"- Medium priority: real-world treatment sequencing after osimertinib, including Velmara versus NX-441.","kind":"bullet","heading":"8. IMPLICATIONS FOR THE EVIDENCE PLAN (PROGRAMME TEAM VIEW)"}],"dropped_reason":null},
{"unit":"u53","blocks":[{"text":"- To explore: PROs and quality of life in frail patients, and caregiver burden.","kind":"bullet","heading":"8. IMPLICATIONS FOR THE EVIDENCE PLAN (PROGRAMME TEAM VIEW)"}],"dropped_reason":null},
{"unit":"u54","blocks":[{"text":"Open questions for the workshop:","kind":"paragraph","heading":"8. IMPLICATIONS FOR THE EVIDENCE PLAN (PROGRAMME TEAM VIEW)"}],"dropped_reason":null},
{"unit":"u55","blocks":[{"text":"1. Can the existing EU5 single-arm chart review be extended with an external comparator arm, or is a new study needed?","kind":"bullet","heading":"8. IMPLICATIONS FOR THE EVIDENCE PLAN (PROGRAMME TEAM VIEW)"}],"dropped_reason":null},
{"unit":"u56","blocks":[{"text":"2. Which US data source gives the fastest credible persistence estimate after launch?","kind":"bullet","heading":"8. IMPLICATIONS FOR THE EVIDENCE PLAN (PROGRAMME TEAM VIEW)"}],"dropped_reason":null},
{"unit":"u57","blocks":[{"text":"3. Is the CNS sub-study large enough to support an intracranial claim with payers, or only with clinicians?","kind":"bullet","heading":"8. IMPLICATIONS FOR THE EVIDENCE PLAN (PROGRAMME TEAM VIEW)"}],"dropped_reason":null},
{"unit":"u58","blocks":[],"dropped_reason":"End-of-document marker; no content."}
]}

{"gap_id":"GAP-001","verdict":"accept","confidence":70,"reason":"TAC-006 asks for procedure-level direct costs after recurrence in routine practice, which is the CEA input the gap names. The unstated TKI-progression population is flagged as partial, and TAC-004 is correctly not_relevant."},
{"gap_id":"GAP-002","verdict":"accept","confidence":72,"reason":"TAC-006 explicitly covers HCRU including hospitalisations and ED use after recurrence in routine practice. Outpatient use falls under the general HCRU wording. TAC-020 is rightly limited."},
{"gap_id":"GAP-013","verdict":"accept","confidence":78,"reason":"No tactic states re-biopsy or liquid biopsy at progression, or community stratification, as an outcome. The not_relevant calls and the open status are consistent."},
{"gap_id":"GAP-004","verdict":"accept","confidence":70,"reason":"TAC-013 targets QoL in older and frail patients, but a survey is weaker than validated PRO data for HTA, so partial is justified. The registry is not frailty-specific, so limited fits."},
{"gap_id":"GAP-005","verdict":"accept","confidence":62,"reason":"TAC-013 directly measures caregiver burden in older and frail EGFR TKI patients, and a survey is a standard way to collect it. The partial methodology and unknown EU5 geography are flagged for the protocol."},
{"gap_id":"GAP-006","verdict":"accept","confidence":90,"reason":"TAC-008 matches the US claims source, the six-month persistence and discontinuation outcomes, and the P&T request on every dimension. The registry is correctly limited."},
{"gap_id":"GAP-009","verdict":"accept","confidence":70,"reason":"The sub-study and real-world CNS evidence cover intracranial response and duration, but the small sample leaves adequacy for a payer claim unproven. Partial coverage and partially_addressed status are appropriate."},
{"gap_id":"GAP-008","verdict":"accept","confidence":80,"reason":"TAC-009 directly matches the post-osimertinib population and the velmaratinib, NX-441 and chemotherapy sequencing. The registry and natural-history study are appropriately supporting only."},
{"gap_id":"GAP-003","verdict":"accept","confidence":75,"reason":"TAC-007 is the only tactic with both the elderly population and the regional SoC comparator, but its design, power and EU5 coverage are unproven, so partial is right. The context tactics are correctly limited."},
{"gap_id":"GAP-007","verdict":"accept","confidence":68,"reason":"TAC-014 covers community-site ILD and QT management but does not state discontinuation as an outcome, so partial is right. The other tactics are correctly limited."},
{"gap_id":"GAP-010","verdict":"accept","confidence":78,"reason":"TAC-012 gives the by-arm count of radiotherapy for new brain lesions in VEL-301, which is exactly what the gap asks. Cost translation is a separate modelling step."},
{"gap_id":"GAP-011","verdict":"accept","confidence":82,"reason":"TAC-014 measures real-world ILD incidence and time to onset directly. The registry is a reasonable partial supporting mapping."},
{"gap_id":"GAP-012","verdict":"accept","confidence":62,"reason":"TAC-014 addresses QT at community sites with less consistent monitoring, but ECG adherence is not a stated outcome. Partial is generous (limited would be defensible), but the partially_addressed status holds either way."},
{"gap_id":"GAP-014","verdict":"accept","confidence":75,"reason":"No tactic specifies a validated frailty score or reports clinical outcomes by frailty. The not_relevant mappings and the open status are consistent."}
]}

{"gap_id":"GAP-013","verdict":"keep","confidence":55,"note":"TAC-020 is the only tactic that could plausibly capture re-biopsy or liquid biopsy after osimertinib progression. {"gap_id":"GAP-005","verdict":"revise","confidence":60,"note":"TAC-013 should be partial, not full. EU5 geography, the caregiver instruments, and the comparator are all unconfirmed. Status should become partially_addressed.","mappings":[{"tactic_id":"TAC-013","verdict":"revise","note":"Change coverage from full to partial. {"gap_id":"GAP-009","verdict":"keep","confidence":62,"note":"Partial coverage from the sub-study, the pooled analysis and the real-world study, plus limited support from VEL-201, is a fair reading. {"gap_id":"GAP-006","verdict":"keep","confidence":78,"note":"TAC-008 matches the P&T request for claims-based six-month persistence and discontinuation, so 'addressed' holds. {"gap_id":"GAP-003","verdict":"revise","confidence":55,"note":"The gap asks for a powered or properly adjusted comparison. {"gap_id":"GAP-001","verdict":"revise","confidence":62,"note":"TAC-006 should be 'partial', not 'full'. {"gap_id":"GAP-013","verdict":"keep","confidence":50,"note":"Only TAC-020 could plausibly capture re-biopsy or liquid biopsy at osimertinib progression, and 'limited' reflects that it is not stated as an outcome or by setting. {"gap_id":"GAP-005","verdict":"keep","confidence":65,"note":"TAC-013 targets caregiver burden in older and frail patients. {"gap_id":"GAP-009","verdict":"keep","confidence":62,"note":"The sub-study, the pooled VEL-201/VEL-301 analysis and the real-world CNS evidence enlarge the sample, while VEL-201 is only supportive. {"gap_id":"GAP-006","verdict":"keep","confidence":78,"note":"TAC-008 matches the US claims-based six-month persistence and discontinuation request, so 'full' and addressed are supported. {"gap_id":"GAP-003","verdict":"keep","confidence":64,"note":"TAC-007 has the right elderly population and regional SoC comparator but its power and adjustment are unspecified, so 'partial' is right. {"gap_id":"GAP-007","verdict":"keep","confidence":55,"note":"TAC-014 is the best fit, covering ILD and QT at community sites, but discontinuation is not a named outcome, so 'partial' is right. {"gap_id":"GAP-013","verdict":"accept","confidence":60,"reason":"Only TAC-020 could plausibly capture re-biopsy at osimertinib progression, and 'limited' with partially_addressed reflects that this is speculative. {"gap_id":"GAP-005","verdict":"accept","confidence":82,"reason":"TAC-013 targets caregiver burden in older and frail patients. Unconfirmed EU5 geography, instruments and HTA weight justify partial coverage and partially_addressed."},

{"gap_id":"GAP-006","verdict":"accept","confidence":85,"reason":"TAC-008 matches the US claims-based six-month persistence and discontinuation request on geography, source and outcome. Full coverage and addressed are defensible, with the registry as supportive only."},
{"gap_id":"GAP-003","verdict":"accept","confidence":84,"reason":"TAC-007 has the elderly population and regional SoC comparator but its power and adjustment are unspecified, so partial is right. The other tactics are correctly limited, and partially_addressed follows."},
{"gap_id":"GAP-007","verdict":"accept","confidence":80,"reason":"TAC-014 covers ILD and QT at community sites but does not name discontinuation as an outcome, so partial is fair. The remaining tactics are indirect, giving partially_addressed."},
{"gap_id":"GAP-010","verdict":"accept","confidence":86,"reason":"TAC-012 counts radiotherapy for new brain lesions by VEL-301 arm, which is the quantity the gap asks for. Cost translation is a separate downstream step, so full and addressed hold."},
{"gap_id":"GAP-014","verdict":"accept","confidence":60,"reason":"Only the registry could provide outcomes in frail patients, and only if a validated frailty score is collected, so 'limited' and partially_addressed are consistent. {"gap_id":"GAP-004","verdict":"accept","confidence":82,"reason":"TAC-013 targets QoL in frail patients, but its instruments and methodology are unconfirmed. The registry collects PROs without targeting frail patients, so partial coverage and partially_addressed are fair."},

{"gap_id":"GAP-011","verdict":"accept","confidence":84,"reason":"TAC-014 targets real-world ILD incidence, time to onset and management, so full coverage and addressed are supported. The registry is an appropriate supportive source."},
{"gap_id":"GAP-012","verdict":"accept","confidence":80,"reason":"TAC-014 covers QT management at community sites but does not measure ECG monitoring adherence, so partial is right. The registry is only limited support, giving partially_addressed."}

The 3-month lag covers independent statistical review, bias analyses and HTA-ready reporting.","withdraw":false,"withdraw_reason":""},{"id":"GAP-023:proposal:2","gap_id":"GAP-023","name":"Elderly MAIC of VEL-301 versus published single-agent chemotherapy data","type":"maic","evidence_question":"After matching baseline characteristics, how do progression-free and overall survival in VEL-301 patients aged 65 and over compare with published outcomes of single-agent chemotherapy in older patients with EGFR-mutant NSCLC after osimertinib?","rationale":"A MAIC reweights VEL-301 individual patient data to published comparator aggregate data. It is cheaper and faster (about 3-4 months) and needs no data licence. It does not duplicate TAC-002, which is descriptive and unadjusted. It could be ready near the 2027-01-15 deadline but this is not guaranteed, and it is a stopgap rather than a replacement for TAC-007.","population":"VEL-301 participants aged 65 and over (individual patient data), weighted to match published cohorts of older adults with EGFR-mutant NSCLC after osimertinib treated with single-agent chemotherapy","comparator":"Published single-agent chemotherapy cohorts in older or post-osimertinib EGFR-mutant NSCLC identified by a targeted literature review (aggregate data only)","outcomes":"Progression-free survival and overall survival hazard ratios, with effective sample size after weighting, covariate balance and sensitivity to unmeasured confounding","data_source":"VEL-301 individual patient data for patients aged 65 and over; published trials and observational cohorts from a targeted literature search","study_design":"Unanchored MAIC with propensity-based weighting on prognostic covariates, a pre-specified covariate list, a targeted literature review for comparator selection, and scenario and quantitative bias analyses, following HTA indirect-comparison guidance","duration_months":3,"readout_lag_months":1,"timing_rationale":"No new data collection is needed, only a targeted literature search, covariate selection and weighting on an existing VEL-301 data cut, about 3 months. The 1-month lag covers QC and report writing for HTA submission.","withdraw":false,"withdraw_reason":""}]}

calls.reply: {"tactics":[{"id":"GAP-001:proposal:1","gap_id":"GAP-001","name":"Procedure-level recurrence cost module (US claims plus EU5 tariff mapping) within the HCRU study","type":"hcru_study","evidence_question":"What are the payer-perspective direct costs, by procedure category, of managing recurrence after progression on a third-generation EGFR TKI in routine US and EU5 practice?","rationale":"The CEA needs recurrence costs broken down by procedure. calls.reply: {"tactics":[{"id":"GAP-027:proposal:1","gap_id":"GAP-027","name":"Frail-patient HTA-grade PRO stratum in the prospective Velmara registry","type":"registry","evidence_question":"What are the health-related quality of life, symptom and functional outcomes over 12 months, measured with HTA-accepted instruments, in frail patients starting Velmara in routine care, compared with non-frail registry patients?","rationale":"The registry (TAC-021) is planned, so a pre-specified frail stratum with a fixed HTA-grade PRO schedule can be built in before first patient in. Missing data handled by MMRM with pattern-mixture sensitivity analyses. Utilities reported in a form usable for the cost-effectiveness model (TAC-004).","instrument":"EORTC QLQ-C30, QLQ-LC13, EQ-5D-5L, G8 screening tool, Zarit Burden Interview short form (caregiver)","study_design":"Pre-specified frailty-enriched stratum within the prospective multinational observational registry. Caregiver-assisted completion is permitted and flagged.","gap_coverage":"Closes the missing frail-specific, Velmara-specific, HTA-grade PRO evidence by adding a counting stratum to an accepted registry. Has no randomised comparator, so it describes frail patients and compares them with non-frail registry patients only.","cost_effort":"Moderate incremental cost on top of the registry: PRO platform licences, frailty screening, enrichment quota and extra site monitoring. Real-world frailty assessment varies.","post_hoc":"","prospective_enrolment":"Yes: prospective enrolment of a frailty-enriched stratum of about 150 patients","protocol_amendment":"Needed: a design addition to the planned registry protocol before first patient in, plus ethics submissions. It is non-randomised and lacks an external comparator. Cost/effort: much cheaper than a new study because it shares sites, data capture and governance. Time: slower to read out than a survey, but TAC-021 is not yet running, so adding the stratum now delays nothing. Feasibility: depends on the registry launching on schedule and on achieving the frail quota. A dedicated prospective cohort with a contemporaneous comparator fills this directly.","proposal_kind":"new","target_tactic_id":null,"expansion_scope":null,"comparative_rationale":"Evidence quality: higher than the registry stratum for comparative questions, because a contemporaneous comparator arm is built in and adjusted with IPTW. Cost/effort: higher than the registry stratum because it needs separate sites, contracts, an ethics package and an independent PRO platform. Time: runs independently of the registry start, so it can begin sooner at selected EU5 and US sites, but still reads out after the 2027-03-31 decision date. Feasibility: recruiting a comparator arm of frail patients is difficult and depends on regional standard of care, but TAC-013 and the EU5 chart-review sites can be used for site selection. It is distinct from TAC-013, which is a non-counting experience survey and not Velmara-specific, and from TAC-021, which has no comparator. Expanding TAC-021 is the cheaper alternative and is proposed as the other candidate.","population":"Adults with EGFR-mutant advanced NSCLC progressing on osimertinib who are frail (G8 score ≤14 or ECOG PS 2) and starting Velmara or a regional standard-of-care regimen (platinum chemotherapy or NX-441 where available), about 120 per arm across US and EU5","comparator":"Frail patients starting regional standard of care (platinum-based chemotherapy or NX-441 where available), contemporaneous, adjusted by IPTW","outcomes":"Primary: change from baseline to 6 months in EORTC QLQ-C30 global health status. Secondary: EQ-5D-5L utility, QLQ-LC13 symptoms, time to deterioration, Zarit caregiver burden, ADL/IADL function, treatment discontinuation and PRO completion rates","data_source":"Primary prospective PRO collection at about 30 sites (academic and community) in US and EU5, with linked treatment and clinical data from medical records","study_design":"Prospective, multicentre, non-interventional comparative cohort study. Frailty is screened at enrolment (G8, ECOG). PROs are collected at baseline, 1, 3 and 6 months by an electronic platform with caregiver-assist options. Analysis uses IPTW on pre-specified confounders (age, ECOG, brain metastases, prior lines, comorbidity) with MMRM for PRO change, E-value sensitivity analyses and tipping-point analyses for missing data.","duration_months":24,"readout_lag_months":4,"timing_rationale":"Site start-up and approvals in about 4 months, 14 months of enrolment for about 240 frail patients, and 6 months of PRO follow-up for the last patient give about 24 months. calls.reply: {"tactics":[{"id":"GAP-021:proposal:1","gap_id":"GAP-021","name":"US claims persistence study: staged read-outs, matched comparator cohorts, age and site-type strata","type":"rwe_study","evidence_question":"What are six-month persistence and discontinuation rates for velmaratinib in US routine care compared with matched post-osimertinib comparator cohorts, and how do they differ by age (<65 vs ≥65) and site type (academic vs community)?","rationale":"The parent TAC-008 answers the payer question in principle, but P&T wants early reads, a benchmark and subgroup splits. Adding staged read-outs, matched comparators and strata makes the persistence numbers credible and interpretable without a new study.","proposal_kind":"expansion","target_tactic_id":"TAC-008","expansion_scope":{"name":"US claims persistence study: staged read-outs, matched comparator cohorts, age and site-type strata","evidence_question":"What are six-month persistence and discontinuation rates for velmaratinib in US routine care compared with matched post-osimertinib comparator cohorts, and how do they differ by age (<65 vs ≥65) and site type (academic vs community)?","population":"Adults with EGFR-mutant advanced NSCLC who initiate velmaratinib after osimertinib in US routine care, identified in linked open and closed claims. Matched comparator cohorts are initiators of NX-441, osimertinib re-challenge or platinum-based chemotherapy in the same period. Strata are age <65 vs ≥65 years and academic vs community site type.","outcomes":"Primary: proportion persistent on index therapy at 6 months (60-day permissible gap). Secondary: time to discontinuation, proportion of patients who switch, medication possession ratio/proportion of days covered, time to next treatment, and all-cause mortality as a competing event, each by age and site-type stratum.","geography":"US","data_cut":"Quarterly claims refreshes. Descriptive read-outs at about 3 months, 6 months and 12 months after launch accrual starts. A pre-launch benchmark cut of existing osimertinib and NX-441 second-line persistence in historical claims is available now.","analysis":"New-user, active-comparator cohort design. Propensity-score matching or overlap weighting on age, sex, comorbidity, prior therapy, brain metastasis proxy, payer type and site type. Kaplan-Meier and Cox models for time to discontinuation with competing-risk sensitivity analyses. Stratum-specific estimates with interaction tests. Gap-length sensitivity at 30, 60 and 90 days.","instrument":"Claims-based algorithms for persistence and discontinuation (proportion of days covered, 60-day gap rule), with a validated NSCLC and EGFR-testing proxy algorithm.","study_design":"Retrospective new-user active-comparator cohort in US administrative claims, with pre-specified staged read-outs and a historical benchmark cohort. Matching and weighting are applied separately within each age and site-type stratum.","gap_coverage":"Covers the P&T request for persistence in routine care. Adds comparator context and the age and site-type subgroups that the base study lacks, and early reads for P&T.","cost_effort":"Moderate incremental cost over the base claims study: added data licences for comparator cohorts and stratified analyses, and about 2-3 FTE-months of extra biostatistics.","timing":"Benchmark cohort can read out within about 3 months of start. The first velmaratinib read-out depends on launch uptake. The 6-month persistence read-out lags launch by about 9-10 months including claims run-out.","feasibility_risks":"Small early velmaratinib samples limit stratum precision. Claims lag delays reads. calls.reply: {"reviews":[{"id":"GAP-001:proposal:1","verdict":"revise","confidence":58,"note":"The design is sound: payer-perspective micro-costing of recurrence is the right input for the CEA, and the expansion adds a valid costing scope to TAC-006 rather than duplicating it. The timing does not hold. evidence_available is 2026-11-30, the same day as the CEA input freeze, with no buffer for CEA integration, and start_date is null. With 4 months of work plus a 2-month lag, a start by about May 2026 is needed. Set a start_date and an evidence_available at least 4-6 weeks before the freeze, or define an interim topline cost table for the CEA with the full cut to follow. Claims licence and EU5 centre access are unconfirmed, so state them as a go/no-go milestone in feasibility_risks. Make EU5 limits explicit: tariff mapping is not payer patient-level data. Keep GAP-001:proposal:2 as the fallback if the claims contract slips.","issues":["timing","evidence_available_at_deadline","start_date_missing","data_access_unconfirmed"],"duplicate_of":null},{"id":"GAP-001:proposal:2","verdict":"keep","confidence":66,"note":"This is a credible fast fallback. It does not duplicate TAC-006 (primary routine-practice data) or TAC-004 (the model). An SLR with tariff mapping and a modified Delphi can produce a procedure-level cost table in about 4 months with no data licence, and it can plausibility-check claims-derived costs. Evidence quality is lower: it rests on published and expert-estimated resource use, and literature specific to post-third-generation-TKI recurrence may be sparse. Label it a bridging input, not a replacement. Define Delphi panel composition per country and a consensus threshold. Consider extending the SLR to 3-4 months, since 2 months for search, screening and extraction is tight.","issues":[],"duplicate_of":null},{"id":"GAP-020:proposal:1","verdict":"revise","confidence":55,"note":"This is a valid expansion of TAC-010 and uses the highest-quality data (randomised trial, BICR, RANO-BM). Three things need fixing. (1) Timing: the data_cut rule ('later of 50% events or 12 months from response') is open-ended, and duration 12 plus lag 3 gives about 15 months, which likely misses the 2027-03-31 decision date. Add an earlier interim cut with a pre-stated precision target, and set start_date and evidence_available. (2) Gap coverage: the tactic does not increase sample size, so it quantifies precision but does not close the adequacy concern. Say this in gap_coverage and pair it with TAC-011/TAC-024 or a pooled analysis with VEL-201. (3) Trial integrity: an extra by-arm cut on an ongoing randomised trial needs a firewall and a DMC or independent statistician. State this in feasibility_risks. The protocol amendment is not approved, so list it as a precondition. Keep the by-arm comparison labelled exploratory.","issues":["timing","gap_coverage","data_cut_open_ended","trial_integrity","protocol_amendment_pending"],"duplicate_of":null},{"id":"GAP-020:proposal:2","verdict":"revise","confidence":35,"note":"Adding sample and generalisability is a valid scope for TAC-011, but the design and timeline do not hold. (1) The post-launch timing is incoherent. A mid-2027 launch means no routine-care velmaratinib patients exist yet. Roughly 150 patients with measurable brain metastases cannot accrue in 12 months. Reaching 12-month median follow-up needs follow-up beyond accrual, so 18 months is too short. The final readout would fall well after the 2027-03-31 decision. (2) The study_design 'retrospective-prospective' is ambiguous and conflicts with prospective_enrolment=false. Consecutive patients accrued after launch, with a new protocol, ethics and contracts, is prospective enrolment. Choose retrospective (early-access or named-patient data, VEL-201 extension) or prospective, set the booleans to match, and state the reason in feasibility_risks. (3) Cut the n target to what is realistic, or reframe the study as an interim 6-month cut. Consider embedding it in the TAC-021 registry or pooling with VEL-201 (TAC-024) to avoid a stand-alone study. Add start_date and evidence_available. As written it cannot close the gap before the decision.","issues":["duration","timing","accrual_feasibility","flag_inconsistency","design_ambiguity","start_date_missing"],"duplicate_of":null}]}

calls.reply: {"reviews":[{"id":"GAP-027:proposal:1","verdict":"revise","confidence":62,"note":"A registry module is a credible, low-cost way to get Velmara-specific frail PRO and utility data, and sharing the registry's infrastructure is sensible. The timing fields are inconsistent. The evidence_question and timing_rationale describe a 12-month PRO endpoint, but outcomes names the primary endpoint as change at 12 weeks. Pick one. If the primary endpoint is 12 weeks, shorten duration_months to roughly 15-18 (12 months of enrolment plus about 3 months of follow-up). If 12-month PROs are needed for CEA, keep 24 months and state this as a secondary endpoint. Also fix the frailty definition ('G8 ≤14 and/or ECOG PS 2'). Choose one rule, or specify a G8 screen followed by geriatric assessment, so the frail cohort is not misclassified. The internal frail vs non-frail comparison is descriptive only and gives no comparative evidence against other therapies, which gap_coverage already states. The registry has no start date, so the amendment is really a protocol design change before first patient. Say that explicitly, and do not assume approval.","issues":["timing_inconsistency","endpoint_definition","frailty_definition","comparator"],"duplicate_of":null},{"id":"GAP-027:proposal:2","verdict":"revise","confidence":48,"note":"A concurrent comparator adds value for HTA, but the design needs tightening. (1) The comparator is a heterogeneous mix ('chemotherapy-based regimen or other EGFR-directed therapy'). Name the regional standard-of-care arms, including NX-441 where available, and pre-specify the primary comparison. (2) Duration is optimistic. Start-up of 3 months, enrolment of 9-12 months and 24-week follow-up come to about 18-21 months, so set duration_months to about 21 or justify 18. (3) The Velmara arm cannot enrol before launch, and roughly 100 frail patients per arm with high PRO attrition and confounding by indication is a real risk. Add an attrition assumption, a sample-size justification against the minimal important difference, and a fallback if the Velmara arm is slow. (4) This and the registry-module expansion (proposal 1) overlap on frail PRO collection. State when the stand-alone study would be chosen over the cheaper module, for example only if payers require a comparator. It is not a duplicate of TAC-013, TAC-021 or TAC-007.","issues":["comparator","duration","feasibility","sample_size","overlap_with_expansion"],"duplicate_of":null},{"id":"GAP-029:proposal:1","verdict":"keep","confidence":72,"note":"A retrospective US EHR-derived cohort is a runnable design that fits this gap. It is a valid expansion of TAC-009, with a US geography, named NX-441 and platinum chemotherapy cohorts, and defined pathway, time-on-treatment, rwPFS, OS and CNS outcomes. The 4-month build plus 3-month readout is credible because the data already exist. Watch NX-441 sample size and the 12-month post-availability data cut, so run a feasibility count of NX-441 patients before committing. The Velmara arm should stay a descriptive reference only. Data licence and protocol approval still need to be arranged. No post-hoc, enrolment or amendment constraint applies.","issues":[],"duplicate_of":null},{"id":"GAP-029:proposal:2","verdict":"revise","confidence":50,"note":"EU5 comparator-sequence data is a legitimate need, and manual abstraction gives better progression and CNS detail than an EHR extract. But TAC-009 already lists US+EU5 geography and a Velmara vs NX-441 vs chemotherapy sequencing question, so framing this as a 'new' tactic risks duplicating it. Re-propose it as an EU5 expansion of TAC-009, or explain precisely why it is not covered by TAC-009. The real feasibility risk is NX-441 uptake in EU5. A target of at least 100 NX-441 patients across 15-20 centres may be unattainable if the drug launched recently, so add a feasibility count and a fallback (pool countries, lower the target, or prospective accrual). Keep the 9-month duration only if site contracting and ethics are confirmed at 3-4 months. Clarify the role of elderly and brain-metastasis subgroups, since TAC-003 and TAC-007 already target elderly patients.","issues":["possible_overlap_with_TAC-009","feasibility","sample_size","expansion_vs_new"],"duplicate_of":null}]}

calls.reply: {"tactics":[{"id":"GAP-034:proposal:2","gap_id":"GAP-034","name":"Real-world post-osimertinib control-pathway OS benchmarking study for CEA background survival and hazard-shape plausibility","type":"rwe_study","evidence_question":"What are long-term overall survival, conditional survival and hazard-function shape in real-world patients with EGFR-mutant advanced NSCLC who receive osimertinib re-challenge or investigator's-choice therapy after first-line osimertinib failure in the US and EU5, with at least 36-48 months of potential follow-up, so that the CEA and HTA submissions can benchmark control-arm and background survival and check the plausibility of tail-hazard assumptions?","rationale":"VEL-301 OS will be immature at the 2027-03-31 decision, and the first VEL-301 OS look is the Q4 2027 interim. Payers and HTA bodies will therefore scrutinise the long-term survival extrapolations in the CEA. Real-world OS in patients on the VEL-301 control-type pathways cannot validate velmaratinib curves, because the velmaratinib treatment effect is unknown outside VEL-301. This study instead gives an external anchor for (a) the long-term shape and level of control-pathway survival, (b) conditional survival and background hazard in the modelled tail, and (c) the plausibility of the hazard shapes in the control-arm extrapolation. The velmaratinib effect itself stays tied to VEL-301 and to the interim and mature OS follow-up (TAC-015, TAC-027).","proposal_kind":"new","target_tactic_id":null,"expansion_scope":null,"comparative_rationale":"Evidence quality: non-randomised and descriptive, so lower than adjusted trial OS. It cannot support a velmaratinib efficacy or extrapolation-validation claim. Its value is as a control-pathway and background-survival benchmark with long follow-up, which trial data will not give before 2028 or later. Alternatives considered. (1) Expanding TAC-015 (long-term OS follow-up) would add trial-based evidence of higher quality, but it cannot be read out before the Q4 2027 interim, so it misses the 2027-03-31 decision and the CEA freeze; it is the right vehicle for velmaratinib OS and is not displaced. (2) Expanding TAC-020 (natural history of recurrence) would blur its clinical-burden purpose and add OS-benchmark analysis to a tactic designed for descriptive clinical course. I instead propose a shared cohort build with TAC-020 (common data model, cohort definitions and mortality-linkage work) with a separate protocol and analysis, to save cost. (3) Expanding TAC-021 (prospective registry) would yield OS only after 2028 and from velmaratinib starters, so it is too late for this decision. (4) Expanding TAC-007 (elderly comparative effectiveness) would dilute its comparative purpose; this study only runs elderly and brain-metastasis sensitivity cohorts. Cost and effort: moderate, because it uses existing de-identified or registry data with no enrolment, and sharing infrastructure with TAC-020 reduces cost further. Time: an early US-only data cut can be delivered before the 30 Nov 2026 CEA freeze, and the full multinational readout lands before the 2027-03-31 decision. Feasibility: the main risks are data access (not yet secured), small 2019-2021 post-osimertinib cohorts, because first-line osimertinib uptake was still building, and incomplete EU5 mortality capture. Mitigations are pooling across sources, validating vital status, and dropping the freeze claim for EU5 if linkage slips.","population":"Adults with EGFR-mutant advanced or metastatic NSCLC who progressed on first-line osimertinib and started a VEL-301 control-type second-line pathway, defined as osimertinib re-challenge (with or without chemotherapy) or investigator's-choice therapy such as platinum-based chemotherapy, in the US and EU5. The primary cohort has index dates from 2019-01-01 to 2021-12-31 and a data cut no earlier than 2025-12-31, giving at least 48 months of potential follow-up for every patient (36 months as the minimum acceptable threshold if a source's data cut is earlier). A secondary cohort with index dates in 2022-2023 contributes early-hazard data only and is not used for tail estimates. Patients who received velmaratinib, NX-441 or other investigational agents, or who were in trials, are excluded where identifiable. Pre-specified sensitivity cohorts are patients aged 65 and over and patients with baseline brain metastases.","comparator":"None — external benchmark. Observed real-world OS is described against published control-arm and real-world survival estimates. It will also be compared with the VEL-301 control-arm OS once that is available (the Q4 2027 interim at the earliest, so not for the 2027-03-31 decision). It is not a head-to-head comparison with velmaratinib, and no velmaratinib curve is validated against it.","outcomes":"Primary: OS from start of second-line therapy at 12, 24, 36 and 48 months, median OS, and restricted mean survival time at 36 and 48 months. Secondary: conditional survival (for example OS at 24 months given survival to 12 months), smoothed hazard function over time and its shape (monotone decreasing, plateauing or increasing tail), the pathway-specific split (osimertinib re-challenge versus investigator's choice), and the fit and plausibility of candidate parametric and flexible models for the control pathway against observed tail data. Mortality-capture quality metrics are reported for each source: proportion of deaths captured against a reference, reverse Kaplan-Meier follow-up, and the proportion lost to follow-up.","data_source":"Candidate sources, each subject to access agreements that have not yet been secured. US: a licensed de-identified oncology EHR-derived database with linked commercial and national death-index mortality data. EU5: England (National Disease Registration Service with SACT and ONS mortality linkage); France (ESME-Lung or equivalent, with national death-registry linkage); Germany (a clinical cancer registry such as CRISP, or hospital registry data with vital-status follow-up); Italy (regional administrative health databases with death-registry linkage); Spain (a thoracic tumour registry such as the GECP registry, with vital-status follow-up). Vital-status validation: for each source, compare captured deaths with the national or linked death index, require adequate capture (target 85% or higher) for inclusion in the tail estimates, run sensitivity analyses censoring at last recorded activity, and exclude from tail estimates any source that fails capture validation.","study_design":"Retrospective multinational cohort study with a pre-specified protocol and statistical analysis plan, sharing the cohort build and common data model with TAC-020 but with a separate protocol and outputs. Source-level Kaplan-Meier estimation with random-effects pooling or stratified presentation. Baseline characteristics are weighted to the VEL-301 eligibility criteria with overlap or inverse-probability weights, applied to describe a trial-like population and not to estimate a treatment effect. Smoothed hazard estimation and fitting of parametric and flexible survival models to the observed data, with comparison of tail hazards. Pre-specified sensitivity analyses on capture quality, calendar period, and the elderly and brain-metastasis subgroups. Staged deliverables: (1) an early US-only descriptive cut for the CEA before the 2026-11-30 input freeze, and (2) the full multinational analysis for the HTA and P&T dossiers. Results are written up as a benchmark report, with the caveat that they do not estimate velmaratinib survival.","duration_months":7,"readout_lag_months":2,"timing_rationale":"Proposed start 2026-06-01, conditional on data-access agreements being signed, which has not happened; if access slips past 2026-07-01 the freeze deliverable is dropped and the study supports only the 2027-03-31 decision. Duration of 7 months (to 2026-12-31) covers access and protocol finalisation (months 1-2), shared cohort build and mortality linkage (months 2-5), and completion of EU5 linkage and validation (months 6-7). No enrolment is needed. A US-only early cut is taken around 2026-10-15 (month 4-5) and analysed within about four weeks, so it can be delivered by 2026-11-20 ahead of the 2026-11-30 freeze, and it is restricted to descriptive KM and hazard outputs for the primary cohort. The 2-month readout lag after the last data (2026-12-31) covers pooling, model-fit analysis and report writing, giving a full readout around 2027-02-28, ahead of the 2027-03-31 decision. This leaves about one month of slack and nothing more, so the early cut is the contingency if EU5 linkage is delayed."}]}

calls.reply: {"tactics":[{"id":"GAP-027:proposal:1","gap_id":"GAP-027","name":"Frailty-stratified HTA-grade PRO module within the Velmara registry","type":"registry","evidence_question":"What are health-related quality of life, symptom and caregiver-burden outcomes in frail patients starting Velmara in routine care, with a primary 12-week endpoint and 12-month follow-up for cost-effectiveness utilities, measured with HTA-accepted instruments?","rationale":"The registry (TAC-021) collects PROs but does not target frail patients. A frailty-stratified module with preference-based and cancer-specific instruments gives Velmara-specific frail-patient QoL and utility data for HTA and CEA use. This revision fixes one primary endpoint (12 weeks) with 12 months as a secondary endpoint, and one frailty rule (G8 screen confirmed by geriatric assessment).","proposal_kind":"expansion","target_tactic_id":"TAC-021","expansion_scope":{"name":"Frailty-stratified HTA-grade PRO module within the Velmara registry","evidence_question":"What are health-related quality of life, symptom and caregiver-burden outcomes in frail patients starting Velmara in routine care, with a primary 12-week endpoint and 12-month follow-up for cost-effectiveness utilities, measured with HTA-accepted instruments?","population":"Adults with EGFR-mutant NSCLC starting Velmara in routine care who are frail. Frailty is a single two-step rule: G8 screening score of 14 or less at baseline, confirmed by an abbreviated comprehensive geriatric assessment showing at least one impaired domain (functional, nutritional, cognitive, mood, comorbidity or polypharmacy). ECOG PS is recorded as a covariate and does not define frailty. Target about 150 frail patients across US and EU5 sites, with non-frail registry patients (G8 above 14) as an internal reference group.","outcomes":"Primary: change from baseline in EQ-5D-5L utility and EORTC QLQ-C30 global health status at 12 weeks. Secondary: the same measures at 12 months (for CEA utilities); EORTC QLQ-LC13 symptoms; time to deterioration; EQ-5D-5L utilities by progression status; caregiver burden (EQ-5D proxy and Zarit short form); treatment discontinuation; geriatric assessment change.","geography":"US and EU5 (registry sites, with deliberate inclusion of community sites)","data_cut":"Primary-endpoint cut when the last frail patient reaches 12 weeks; interim 12-month cut 6 months after last enrolment; final cut at 12-month follow-up of the last frail patient","analysis":"Descriptive analysis plus mixed-model repeated-measures analysis of PRO change. Frail vs non-frail comparison is descriptive and adjusted for age, sex, ECOG, line of therapy and CNS involvement. It is not a comparison against other therapies. Health-state utilities prepared in HTA and CEA format. Missing-data sensitivity analyses (multiple imputation, pattern-mixture) given expected attrition.","instrument":"EQ-5D-5L, EORTC QLQ-C30, EORTC QLQ-LC13, G8 screening tool, abbreviated comprehensive geriatric assessment, caregiver EQ-5D proxy and Zarit short form, administered electronically or on paper at baseline, weeks 4, 8 and 12, then every 12 weeks","study_design":"Prospective nested frailty-stratified cohort within the multinational observational registry. Frail patients are identified at enrolment with the G8 screen and confirmatory geriatric assessment. PRO collection is aligned to routine visits. The comparison is internal (frail vs non-frail Velmara patients) and descriptive; there is no external active comparator.","gap_coverage":"Closes the missing Velmara-specific, frail-targeted, HTA-grade PRO and utility evidence. Does not provide frail-patient comparative evidence against other therapies.","cost_effort":"Incremental to the registry: added instruments, a G8 and geriatric assessment step, site training and a larger frail-patient target. Low to moderate relative to a stand-alone study because infrastructure, consent and sites are shared.","timing":"Depends on registry start-up. About 12 months of enrolment after registry start, with the 12-week primary readout about 15 months after start and the 12-month secondary data about 24 months after start. All of this falls after the 2027-03-31 decision date.","feasibility_risks":"The registry is planned with no start date and no patients enrolled, so this is a design change to the draft registry protocol before first patient and ethics submission, not an amendment to a running study. It has not been approved and no approval is assumed. protocol_amendment is flagged true only in that sense. Frail patients are under-represented in registries and have high PRO attrition, so the 12-month secondary endpoint is at most risk. Community site recruitment is uncertain. The frailty rule must be locked in the protocol to avoid misclassification. Geriatric assessment adds site burden.","post_hoc":false,"prospective_enrolment":true,"protocol_amendment":true,"start_date":null,"evidence_available":null},"comparative_rationale":"Evidence quality: a registry module gives prospective, Velmara-specific PRO data in a well-defined frail population, but the internal non-frail comparator is descriptive only. The stand-alone comparative PRO cohort (proposal 2) is stronger because it adds an external comparator. Cost and effort: lowest option, since infrastructure, consent and sites are shared. Time: tied to registry start-up, so not faster than a stand-alone study, and the registry has no start date. Feasibility: moderate, with the risks of registry launch and frail-patient attrition. Rejected options: expanding TAC-013 (a likely cross-sectional survey that is not Velmara-specific or HTA-grade), and a post-hoc VEL-301 frail analysis (frailty screening and HTA-grade PRO collection in the trial are not confirmed).","population":"Adults with EGFR-mutant NSCLC starting Velmara in routine care who are frail (G8 of 14 or less, confirmed by abbreviated comprehensive geriatric assessment); about 150 frail patients in the US and EU5, with non-frail registry patients as an internal reference","comparator":"Internal reference: non-frail Velmara registry patients (descriptive). No external active comparator.","outcomes":"Primary: change from baseline in EQ-5D-5L utility and EORTC QLQ-C30 global health status at 12 weeks. Secondary: 12-month PROs for CEA utilities, QLQ-LC13 symptoms, time to deterioration, utilities by progression status, caregiver burden, discontinuation, geriatric assessment change.","data_source":"Prospective primary data collection within the Velmara registry (electronic PRO and site case report forms)","study_design":"Prospective nested frailty-stratified cohort within the multinational observational registry. Frail patients are identified at enrolment with the G8 screen and confirmatory geriatric assessment. PRO collection is aligned to routine visits. The comparison is internal (frail vs non-frail Velmara patients) and descriptive; there is no external active comparator.","duration_months":24,"readout_lag_months":3,"timing_rationale":"About 12 months of enrolment to reach 150 frail patients, plus 12 months of follow-up for the last patient's 12-month secondary PRO timepoint, so last data arrives about 24 months after start. The 12-week primary endpoint is complete about 15 months after start and can be read out early as an interim analysis. PRO scoring, utility derivation and HTA-format reporting take about 3 months."},{"id":"GAP-027:proposal:2","gap_id":"GAP-027","name":"Prospective comparative HTA-grade PRO cohort in frail patients on Velmara versus standard of care","type":"pro_study","evidence_question":"How do health-related quality of life (EQ-5D-5L utility and EORTC QLQ-C30 global health status) and caregiver burden at 12 weeks compare between frail patients with EGFR-mutant NSCLC starting Velmara and frail patients on regional standard of care?","rationale":"The gap is the lack of frail-patient PRO and QoL evidence that HTA bodies can use. A stand-alone prospective cohort with HTA-accepted instruments and a concurrent standard-of-care comparator gives Velmara-specific utilities and comparative QoL. It does not wait for the registry to start, and it is not a cross-sectional survey like TAC-013.","proposal_kind":"new","target_tactic_id":null,"expansion_scope":null,"comparative_rationale":"Evidence quality: higher than the registry module because it adds a concurrent frail comparator group, with overlap weighting for confounding, though it is still non-randomised. Cost and effort: highest of the options, since it needs its own sites, protocol, ethics approvals and data management. Time: independent of the registry launch and can start as soon as ethics approvals are in place, but enrolment of two arms is slower. Feasibility: moderate; frail-patient recruitment and attrition are the main risks, and the comparator arm is more affected by regional variation in standard of care. The registry expansion (proposal 1) is cheaper but gives only an internal descriptive comparison. A post-hoc VEL-301 analysis was rejected because frailty screening and HTA-grade PRO collection in the trial are not confirmed, and expanding TAC-013 was rejected because it is neither Velmara-specific nor HTA-grade.","population":"Adults with EGFR-mutant advanced NSCLC who are frail (G8 of 14 or less, confirmed by abbreviated comprehensive geriatric assessment showing at least one impaired domain) and are starting second-line or later therapy at US and EU5 academic and community sites. Target about 100 on Velmara and 100 on standard of care, plus a caregiver for each patient where available.","comparator":"Concurrent frail patients starting regional standard of care in the same setting (osimertinib re-challenge, platinum-based chemotherapy or other EGFR TKI as chosen by the treating physician), compared with overlap weighting on baseline covariates.","outcomes":"Primary: change from baseline in EQ-5D-5L utility and EORTC QLQ-C30 global health status at 12 weeks. Secondary: EORTC QLQ-LC13 symptoms, time to deterioration, EQ-5D-5L utilities by progression status for CEA, caregiver burden (EQ-5D proxy, Zarit short form), treatment discontinuation, geriatric assessment change, and PRO at 24 weeks.","data_source":"Prospective primary data collection at US and EU5 sites (electronic PRO, site case report forms and geriatric assessment forms)","study_design":"Prospective, multicentre, non-interventional comparative cohort. Frail patients are screened with G8 and confirmed by abbreviated geriatric assessment at treatment start. PROs are collected at baseline, weeks 4, 8, 12 and 24. Analysis uses mixed-model repeated-measures with overlap weighting on age, sex, ECOG, CNS involvement, comorbidity and line of therapy. Missing data are handled by multiple imputation with pattern-mixture sensitivity analyses. Utilities by health state are prepared in HTA and CEA format. A pre-specified statistical analysis plan is registered before database lock.","duration_months":21,"readout_lag_months":4,"timing_rationale":"About 6 months for protocol, ethics approvals and site activation, about 12 months of enrolment for about 200 frail patients, and 3 months for the last patient's 12-week primary endpoint, so the primary last data arrives about 21 months after start. The 24-week secondary endpoint would extend this by about 3 months, as an interim readout of the primary is possible first. Weighting analysis, utility derivation and HTA-format reporting take about 4 months."}]}

calls.reply: {"reviews":[{"id":"GAP-034:proposal:1","verdict":"keep","confidence":78,"note":"Keep. Expanding TAC-015 is a valid added scope: pre-specified OS cuts, maturity triggers and crossover-adjusted analyses on enrolled VEL-301 patients, with no new enrolment. It is the only option that gives randomised mature OS, and it is more credible than a real-world substitute. Three fixes to make before finalising. (1) data_cut says the final cut is at the earlier of 60% maturity or 5 years after last patient randomised, but duration_months is 48. Align the two, or state that 48 months runs from the amendment. (2) RPSFT and IPCW only apply if control-arm patients switch to velmaratinib or other active therapy. Confirm that VEL-301 permits crossover and that switch data are collected, otherwise rename this as subsequent-therapy adjustment. (3) State that the OS analysis plan is locked before any unblinded OS look. The amendment is unapproved, so the plan should say so and name a target approval date before the Q4 2027 interim. It cannot deliver mature OS by 2027-03-31, but it does provide the committed follow-up plan the gap asks for.","issues":["duration_inconsistency","crossover_assumption_unverified"],"duplicate_of":null},{"id":"GAP-034:proposal:2","verdict":"revise","confidence":35,"note":"Revise. (1) Gap fit: the gap is mature Velmara OS and a follow-up plan. This study gives control-pathway benchmark survival only, so it supports CEA tail plausibility, not the gap itself. Re-label it as supporting evidence for the CEA. (2) Overlap: the population (EGFR-mutant NSCLC after osimertinib) and the survival and clinical-course outcomes largely overlap TAC-020. A shared cohort build is the right instinct, but a separate protocol for the same cohort is hard to justify. Make it an expansion of TAC-020 with the OS-benchmark scope added, or show clearly what is new. (3) Feasibility and timing: the data-access agreements are not secured, and the plan assumes six EU5 and US sources are accessed, linked, validated and analysed in 7 months from 2026-06-01. EU registry and linkage approvals (e.g. NDRS, ESME, Italian regional data) usually take 6–12 months. Make US-only the committed deliverable for the 2026-11-30 freeze and treat EU5 as a later phase, with the duration extended to about 12 months and the full readout after 2027-03-31. (4) Population validity: patients with osimertinib first-line index dates in 2019–2021 who progressed by the data cut are fast progressors, and the cohort will be small and selected. Osimertinib re-challenge is also not standard care after osimertinib failure. Pre-specify expected cohort sizes per source, and justify the control definition against how VEL-301 defines the control arm.","issues":["gap_fit","overlap_TAC-020","data_access","duration","selection_bias","comparator"],"duplicate_of":null}]}

calls.reply: {"reviews":[{"id":"GAP-027:proposal:1","verdict":"keep","confidence":72,"note":"The design is runnable and matches the gap. It is a prospective frail-targeted cohort nested in TAC-021 with a single frailty rule (G8 ≤14 plus geriatric assessment, ≥2 impaired domains). It uses HTA-accepted instruments (EQ-5D-5L, QLQ-C30/LC13) and has a 12-week primary endpoint, with 12-month outcomes for CEA. The 24-month duration and 3-month lag are credible. The limits are stated: the comparison is internal and descriptive only, and the module depends on registry start-up. Two tightenings before the protocol is fixed: specify the non-frail reference group size and the planned attrition handling at 12 months, and confirm ethics approval is obtained before first patient in, since none is assumed. This is a valid expansion of TAC-021, not a duplicate, because it adds frail targeting and HTA-grade PRO and utility scope.","issues":[],"duplicate_of":null},{"id":"GAP-027:proposal:2","verdict":"revise","confidence":48,"note":"Fix the arm arithmetic in `population` and `comparator`. Total n≈200 with '~100 per arm' implies two arms, but three arms are named (Velmara, platinum, NX-441). If platinum and NX-441 split the comparator half, the primary Velmara vs platinum comparison falls below the ~100 per arm that the power calculation assumes. The power calculation itself is correct (about 70 per arm before attrition). Either raise the target to about 100 Velmara, about 100 platinum and at least 40 NX-441 (about 240 total), or drop NX-441 to a descriptive reference. The rationale also needs support: it should be chosen over the registry module only if payers require a comparator, and a decision that depends on that is not yet evidenced. Confounding by indication is a real risk, since frail patients given an oral TKI differ from those given platinum doublet. Add a pre-specified overlap and positivity check and a minimum Velmara enrolment trigger tied to the launch date. The 12-month recruitment assumption is optimistic for a post-launch frail population, so state it as a risk and keep the fallback to the registry module. This tactic is not a duplicate of TAC-013, TAC-021 or TAC-007.","issues":["sample_size_arms","comparator","feasibility","confounding"],"duplicate_of":null},{"id":"GAP-029:proposal:1","verdict":"keep","confidence":70,"note":"A retrospective US EHR-derived cohort is a runnable and fast way to describe NX-441 and platinum pathways after osimertinib, with Velmara as a descriptive reference. The 4-month build plus 3-month lag is credible with no enrolment. Using IPTW, E-values and descriptive Velmara comparisons is appropriately cautious. It is a valid US-scoped expansion of TAC-009, which has no named comparator cohorts. Before commitment, run a cohort-size feasibility count for NX-441, since the data cut is tied to 'at least 12 months after NX-441 availability' and uptake may be small. Name the database and confirm licence and protocol approval. Pre-specify that rwPFS is exploratory given incomplete progression capture, with time on treatment and time to next treatment as the more robust endpoints.","issues":[],"duplicate_of":null},{"id":"GAP-029:proposal:2","verdict":"revise","confidence":55,"note":"The EU5 chart-review expansion of TAC-009 is a reasonable complement to the US database study, but the design has internal inconsistencies. (1) `study_design` says 'consecutive patient selection' but also 'platinum patients sampled to match NX-441 by centre'. Pick one: consecutive for both cohorts, with matching handled at analysis. (2) The target of ~300 with ≥100 platinum and ≥60 NX-441 is not reconciled, so state the intended cohort split. (3) `duration_months` is 10 but the timing rationale says 'the 9-month duration is kept only if...'. Align both to 10 months. (4) The prospective-accrual fallback needs new ethics approval, which conflicts with prospective_enrolment=false and protocol_amendment=false. Either remove the fallback or flag it as a conditional prospective scope in feasibility_risks. (5) 60 NX-441 patients across 15-20 EU5 centres is the main feasibility risk, so make the 6-week feasibility count a hard go/no-go gate. The elderly and CNS subgroups are valid as comparator-arm context and do not duplicate TAC-003 or TAC-007.","issues":["internal_inconsistency","duration","sample_size","prospective_fallback_flags","feasibility"],"duplicate_of":null}]}

calls.reply: {"reviews":[{"id":"GAP-021:proposal:1","verdict":"keep","confidence":72,"note":"Sound expansion of TAC-008. The line-defined benchmark and quarterly cuts are a valid added scope that adds little cost and no amendment or enrolment. The proposal is candid that Velmara-specific 6-month rates cannot exist before about 9 months after launch (usable read-out about 12 months), and that only the benchmark can serve the pre-launch P&T date.
