calls.reply: {"tactics":[{"id":"GAP-021:proposal:1","gap_id":"GAP-021","name":"TAC-008 expansion: US claims persistence with comparator benchmark cohorts and Medicare 65+ stratification","type":"rwe_study","evidence_question":"How do six-month persistence and discontinuation for Velmara compare with those of NX-441, osimertinib re-challenge and platinum chemotherapy after osimertinib failure in US claims, overall and in patients aged 65 and over?","rationale":"Payers distrust trial persistence and want routine-care persistence. A Velmara-only rate has no yardstick, because P&T reviewers need to see it next to the alternatives they already manage. Adding comparator cohorts and an age 65+ stratum to the planned claims study makes the rate interpretable and supports the elderly positioning against NX-441.","proposal_kind":"expansion","target_tactic_id":"TAC-008","expansion_scope":{"name":"TAC-008 expansion: US claims persistence with comparator benchmark cohorts and Medicare 65+ stratification","evidence_question":"How do six-month persistence and discontinuation for Velmara compare with those of NX-441, osimertinib re-challenge and platinum chemotherapy after osimertinib failure in US claims, overall and in patients aged 65 and over?","population":"Adults with EGFR-mutant advanced NSCLC who start a new line of therapy after osimertinib in US claims. Velmara initiators form the index cohort. New initiators of NX-441, osimertinib re-challenge or platinum chemotherapy form the benchmark cohorts. Patients aged 65 and over (Medicare Advantage/FFS) form a pre-specified stratum.","outcomes":"Primary: proportion persistent at 6 months with a 60-day permissible gap. Secondary: time to discontinuation or switch (Kaplan-Meier), proportion of days covered, discontinuation and switching patterns, and the same measures in the 65+ stratum.","geography":"US","data_cut":"Pre-launch cut: comparator-only benchmark cohorts from existing claims history, before launch. Post-launch cuts: first Velmara cohort once initiators have 6 months of follow-up and claims run-out, then refreshed every 6 months.","analysis":"Propensity-score/IPTW adjustment for age, sex, comorbidity, prior therapy, brain metastases proxy and payer type. Kaplan-Meier with adjusted Cox models. Sensitivity analyses with 30-day and 90-day gap definitions.","instrument":"","study_design":"Retrospective, new-user, active-comparator cohort study in a US longitudinal pharmacy and medical claims database, with an index date at first dispense and at least 6 months of follow-up. Persistence is defined from dispensing records. Lung cancer and EGFR status are identified by algorithm, using a linked testing-record subset where available. The 65+ stratum is analysed as a pre-specified subgroup.","gap_coverage":"Covers the payer ask for claims-based six-month persistence and discontinuation. Adds comparative context and an elderly stratum that Velmara-only reporting would lack.","cost_effort":"Moderate incremental cost over the parent: extra cohort build, confounding adjustment and statistical analysis, with no new data purchase beyond the licence the parent already needs. Much lower than a prospective study.","timing":"The comparator benchmark can be ready before launch. The Velmara 6-month persistence cannot be reported before the 2027-03-31 decision, because Velmara claims only start accruing at the 2027-H1 launch. The first post-launch cut is expected roughly 12 to 15 months after launch.","feasibility_risks":"Few Velmara patients early after launch gives imprecise estimates, and the 65+ stratum will be smaller still. Claims have no EGFR status or line of therapy, so identification relies on algorithms, and NX-441 uptake may be low. Comparator confounding by indication is only partly controlled. Claims run-out lags delay each cut. This is a secondary-data study, so there is no enrolment, no trial amendment and no post-hoc trial analysis. The parent protocol is still proposed and the added scope must be written into it, and database access and licensing are not yet confirmed.","post_hoc":false,"prospective_enrolment":false,"protocol_amendment":false,"start_date":null,"evidence_available":"Comparator-cohort claims history is already available in licensed US claims databases, subject to licensing. No Velmara claims exist before launch."},"comparative_rationale":"Expansion versus a new standalone study. A new study would duplicate TAC-008 and repeat the data licence, protocol and ethics work. The expansion reuses the same claims infrastructure and adds comparator and age context for a moderate incremental cost. Evidence quality is moderate: non-randomised and algorithm-based, but adjusted and comparative, which is better than a descriptive Velmara-only rate. Speed is the same as the parent, because the limit is follow-up after launch. Feasibility is high, because no enrolment or amendment is needed. The main risk is small early numbers. A prospective registry module would add PRO-based adherence reasons but is slower and costlier, and is already covered by TAC-021.","population":"Adults with EGFR-mutant advanced NSCLC who start a new line of therapy after osimertinib in US claims. Velmara initiators form the index cohort. New initiators of NX-441, osimertinib re-challenge or platinum chemotherapy form the benchmark cohorts. Patients aged 65 and over (Medicare Advantage/FFS) form a pre-specified stratum.","comparator":"NX-441, osimertinib re-challenge and platinum chemotherapy new-user cohorts after osimertinib failure","outcomes":"Primary: proportion persistent at 6 months with a 60-day permissible gap. Secondary: time to discontinuation or switch (Kaplan-Meier), proportion of days covered, discontinuation and switching patterns, and the same measures in the 65+ stratum.","data_source":"Licensed US longitudinal pharmacy and medical claims database (commercial, Medicare Advantage and FFS), subject to licence confirmation","study_design":"Retrospective, new-user, active-comparator cohort study in a US longitudinal pharmacy and medical claims database, with an index date at first dispense and at least 6 months of follow-up. Persistence is defined from dispensing records. Lung cancer and EGFR status are identified by algorithm, using a linked testing-record subset where available. The 65+ stratum is analysed as a pre-specified subgroup.","duration_months":15,"readout_lag_months":4,"timing_rationale":"Velmara initiators accrue over about 9 months after the 2027-H1 launch, and the last of them needs 6 months of follow-up, giving about 15 months of data accrual. Claims run-out, cleaning, algorithm validation and adjusted analysis add about 4 months. The comparator-only benchmark can be read out earlier, before launch.","withdraw":false,"withdraw_reason":""},{"id":"GAP-021:proposal:2","gap_id":"GAP-021","name":"US specialty pharmacy dispensing early-read persistence analysis for Velmara","type":"rwe_study","evidence_question":"What are early fill-based persistence and discontinuation rates for Velmara in the first months after US launch, using specialty pharmacy dispensing data, and how do they relate to later claims-based persistence?","rationale":"The decision falls at or before launch and claims data lag several months. Oral oncolytics are mostly dispensed through specialty pharmacies, whose dispensing data arrive weeks after a fill. An early, descriptive fill-based persistence readout can give P&T committees an early signal, and an interim 3-month readout can be provided as a post-launch update. A later alignment check against claims links it to the planned claims study.","proposal_kind":"new","target_tactic_id":null,"expansion_scope":null,"comparative_rationale":"A new tactic versus expanding TAC-008. Expanding TAC-008 would inherit its claims run-out lag, which prevents any early signal, and the early dispensing feed differs in source and timing, so it is kept as a separate tactic. It is a distinct data source and purpose, not a repeat of the claims study. Evidence quality is lower than claims: it is descriptive, covers only participating specialty pharmacy channels, has no comparator and lacks clinical covariates. Incremental cost is low to moderate, mainly a data feed and an analysis. It is faster, with a 3-month fill-based persistence readout available within weeks of the data cut. Feasibility depends on securing a specialty pharmacy or hub data partnership, which is not yet confirmed. It complements and does not replace the claims-based study.","population":"Adults with a Velmara dispense in the US specialty pharmacy or hub dispensing feed, with a diagnosis of EGFR-mutant NSCLC where recorded, from first launch fill onward.","comparator":"None — descriptive; published osimertinib persistence used only as an informal external reference","outcomes":"Primary: proportion with continued fills at 3 months and at 6 months using a 45-day gap rule. Secondary: median time to first missed refill, discontinuation, fill intervals, and the proportion of early discontinuations coinciding with dose-modification or hold patterns where recorded. Alignment: concordance of persistence with the later claims-based estimate in the overlapping patients.","data_source":"US specialty pharmacy and hub dispensing data under a data-sharing agreement (not yet confirmed), with later linkage or comparison to the claims database used for TAC-008","study_design":"Descriptive retrospective cohort of Velmara initiators identified from specialty pharmacy dispensing data, with an index date at first fill. Rolling quarterly cuts provide Kaplan-Meier persistence, with a 3-month fill-based interim cut and a 6-month cut once follow-up is complete. A pre-specified alignment analysis compares the dispensing-based estimates with the claims-based estimates in overlapping patients, to show how far they can be trusted. Results are reported by payer type and, where age is recorded, age 65+.","duration_months":12,"readout_lag_months":2,"timing_rationale":"Launch is 2027-H1, and 12 months of data accrual from launch lets the first initiators reach 6 months of follow-up and gives a representative cohort. Dispensing feeds arrive within weeks, so cleaning and analysis take about 2 months per cut. The 3-month interim cut is available well before the 6-month cut, but neither can be reported before the 2027-03-31 decision.","withdraw":false,"withdraw_reason":""}]}

calls.reply: {"tactics":[{"id":"GAP-001:proposal:1","gap_id":"GAP-001","name":"TAC-006 expansion: US claims procedure-level cost of recurrence after third-generation EGFR TKI","type":"hcru_study","evidence_question":"What are the payer-paid direct costs, by procedure category, and associated healthcare resource use in the 12 months after recurrence on a third-generation EGFR TKI in US routine care?","rationale":"The CEA versus osimertinib needs observed, procedure-level US payer costs of recurrence. TAC-006 names this question but has no specified population, data source or design. This expansion makes it a runnable retrospective claims analysis that can read out before the 30 November 2026 CEA and budget-impact input freeze.","proposal_kind":"expansion","target_tactic_id":"TAC-006","expansion_scope":{"name":"TAC-006 expansion: US claims procedure-level cost of recurrence after third-generation EGFR TKI","evidence_question":"What are the payer-paid direct costs, by procedure category, and associated healthcare resource use in the 12 months after recurrence on a third-generation EGFR TKI in US routine care?","population":"Adults (18+) with advanced or metastatic NSCLC and a dispensing of a third-generation EGFR TKI (osimertinib) between 2019 and 2025, with a claims-based recurrence/progression event (next-line systemic therapy switch, new radiotherapy including SRS/WBRT, or re-biopsy/molecular re-testing with treatment change). Continuous enrolment of at least 6 months before the index date. Pre-specified strata: age 65+ versus under 65, and CNS-directed versus non-CNS recurrence.","outcomes":"Primary: mean and median per-patient payer-allowed and plan-paid direct costs in the 6 and 12 months after the recurrence index date, split by procedure category (imaging, biopsy and molecular testing, radiotherapy including SRS, systemic therapy drug and administration, surgery, inpatient stays, ED visits, outpatient visits, supportive and palliative care). Secondary: counts and per-patient-per-month rates of hospitalisations, length of stay, ED visits and procedures; share of patients with CNS-directed procedures; costs by age and CNS stratum.","geography":"US","data_cut":"Latest available quarterly claims refresh, with data complete through at least 2025-12-31","analysis":"Descriptive cost and utilisation estimates with bootstrapped 95% CIs. Gamma-family GLM with log link for adjusted costs. Censoring-adjusted cost estimation for patients who die or disenrol. Costs inflated to a single 2026 USD base year. Outputs formatted as unit costs and event frequencies by CEA health state.","instrument":"","study_design":"Retrospective, descriptive new-user cohort study using licensed US administrative claims (commercial and Medicare). Index date is the claims-defined recurrence event. Follow-up is up to 12 months, ending at death, disenrolment or data cut. No comparator arm; descriptive costing for CEA input.","gap_coverage":"Directly fills the gap: observed US payer procedure-level direct costs of recurrence for the CEA. It gives routine-practice evidence, not modelled or fee-schedule estimates. It covers US only. EU5 costs would need tariff-based or separate country sources.","cost_effort":"Moderate. Needs claims data licence, a protocol and SAP, and biostatistics and epidemiology time. No patient recruitment or site costs. Lower cost than a prospective or linked-EHR design.","timing":"About 3 months from start to data cut and 2 months of analysis, giving a readout of about 5 months. This fits the 30 November 2026 input freeze only if data access and protocol sign-off complete by about end-August 2026.","feasibility_risks":"Claims lack EGFR mutation status and progression dates, so both are proxied by osimertinib use and treatment-change algorithms. This risks misclassification and needs a sensitivity analysis using stricter definitions. CNS procedures may be under-captured. Claims show payer-allowed amounts, not full societal cost. Data licence and access are not yet secured, and nothing here is approved. This is a post-hoc analysis of existing data: no prospective enrolment and no protocol amendment.","post_hoc":false,"prospective_enrolment":false,"protocol_amendment":false,"start_date":null,"evidence_available":null},"comparative_rationale":"Evidence quality: the claims expansion gives observed routine-practice, procedure-level US payer costs, which is the evidence type payers expect. A fee-schedule micro-costing plus SLR (the alternative) is only modelled, so quality is lower. Cost and effort: moderate, and it builds on TAC-006 without a duplicate study. The micro-costing alternative is cheaper but weaker. A prospective HCRU or linked-EHR study would be too slow and costly. Time: about 5 months, which fits the 30 November 2026 freeze if started promptly. Feasibility: depends on claims access and recurrence proxy validity. This is mitigated by sensitivity analyses and by the separate fee-schedule fallback proposal.","population":"Adults (18+) with advanced or metastatic NSCLC and a dispensing of a third-generation EGFR TKI (osimertinib) between 2019 and 2025, with a claims-based recurrence/progression event (next-line systemic therapy switch, new radiotherapy including SRS/WBRT, or re-biopsy/molecular re-testing with treatment change). Continuous enrolment of at least 6 months before the index date. Pre-specified strata: age 65+ versus under 65, and CNS-directed versus non-CNS recurrence.","comparator":"None — descriptive cost analysis; strata compared are age 65+ versus under 65 and CNS versus non-CNS recurrence","outcomes":"Primary: mean and median per-patient payer-allowed and plan-paid direct costs in the 6 and 12 months after the recurrence index date, split by procedure category (imaging, biopsy and molecular testing, radiotherapy including SRS, systemic therapy drug and administration, surgery, inpatient stays, ED visits, outpatient visits, supportive and palliative care). Secondary: counts and per-patient-per-month rates of hospitalisations, length of stay, ED visits and procedures; share of patients with CNS-directed procedures; costs by age and CNS stratum.","data_source":"Licensed US administrative claims database (commercial and Medicare), subject to data access","study_design":"Retrospective, descriptive new-user cohort study using licensed US administrative claims (commercial and Medicare). Index date is the claims-defined recurrence event. Follow-up is up to 12 months, ending at death, disenrolment or data cut. No comparator arm; descriptive costing for CEA input.","duration_months":3,"readout_lag_months":2,"timing_rationale":"The data already exist, so there is no enrolment. About 3 months covers protocol and SAP, data access, cohort build and the final data cut. About 2 months covers cost modelling, QC and a CEA-ready report. This is the minimum credible schedule for the 30 November 2026 freeze.","withdraw":false,"withdraw_reason":""},{"id":"GAP-001:proposal:2","gap_id":"GAP-001","name":"Targeted SLR and fee-schedule micro-costing of recurrence procedures after third-generation EGFR TKI","type":"slr","evidence_question":"What are the unit costs and expected frequencies of the procedures used to manage recurrence after third-generation EGFR TKI progression from a US payer perspective, based on published pathways, CMS fee schedules and clinician validation?","rationale":"This is a fast fallback and complement to the claims study in TAC-006. It builds a transparent, procedure-level cost input for the CEA from published resource-use data and public price files. It does not depend on claims access or recurrence-proxy validity.","proposal_kind":"new","target_tactic_id":null,"expansion_scope":null,"comparative_rationale":"Evidence quality: modelled micro-costing from literature and public fee schedules is lower quality than observed claims costs (the TAC-006 expansion), because it does not reflect actual routine-practice utilisation. Clinician validation partly offsets this. Cost and effort: the lowest option, using desk research and a small panel with no data licence. Time: about 3 months, so it can deliver before the 30 November 2026 freeze with margin. Feasibility: high, because it uses public sources, but published procedure-frequency data after osimertinib are sparse. As a stand-alone it would not give the routine-practice costs the gap asks for, so it is best as a bridge, a validation benchmark and a source for EU5 tariff inputs. It is not a duplicate of TAC-006 because it uses different data, methods and perspective and does not analyse patient-level claims.","population":"Adults with advanced EGFR-mutant NSCLC progressing on a third-generation EGFR TKI (osimertinib), including CNS and non-CNS recurrence, as described in published studies and clinical pathways; US payer perspective, with EU5 tariffs as secondary extraction.","comparator":"None — descriptive costing and evidence synthesis","outcomes":"Unit cost per recurrence-related procedure (imaging, biopsy and molecular re-testing, radiotherapy including SRS, drug administration, surgery, hospital admission, ED visit, supportive care); published frequency of each procedure per recurrence episode; expected direct cost per recurrence episode with low-high ranges; evidence-gap table by procedure.","data_source":"PubMed/Embase and ISPOR/ASCO/WCLC abstract searches; CMS Physician Fee Schedule, OPPS, IPPS/MS-DRG and ASP pricing files; EU5 national tariff schedules; structured validation panel of US oncologists and payer/pharmacy experts","study_design":"Targeted systematic literature review of cost-of-illness and resource-use studies after third-generation EGFR TKI progression, with dual-reviewer screening and extraction. Followed by bottom-up micro-costing: map procedures to CPT/HCPCS/DRG codes and apply CMS fee-schedule rates. Pathway frequencies are validated and gaps filled through a modified-Delphi panel of about 6 clinicians. One-way and probabilistic sensitivity ranges are provided for the CEA.","duration_months":2,"readout_lag_months":1,"timing_rationale":"Searching, screening and extraction take about 2 months, run in parallel with fee-schedule mapping and the clinician panel. About 1 month then covers synthesis, costing and a CEA-ready input table. Public sources and a small panel keep the schedule short.","withdraw":false,"withdraw_reason":""}]}

calls.reply: {"tactics":[{"id":"GAP-020:proposal:1","gap_id":"GAP-020","name":"VEL-301 CNS sub-study: BICR RANO-BM intracranial response with extended MRI follow-up and pre-specified precision targets","type":"subgroup_analysis","evidence_question":"Do blinded-independent-review intracranial response rate and duration of intracranial response in VEL-301 patients with measurable brain metastases reach pre-specified precision and follow-up maturity thresholds that support a durability claim?","rationale":"The sub-study's size cannot be changed cheaply, but how precise and mature its estimates are can be. Central blinded review, brain MRI that continues until intracranial progression, and a pre-specified estimation plan can narrow the interval around duration of response (DoR) and show payers how reliable it is.","proposal_kind":"expansion","target_tactic_id":"TAC-010","expansion_scope":{"name":"VEL-301 CNS sub-study: BICR RANO-BM intracranial response with extended MRI follow-up and pre-specified precision targets","evidence_question":"Do blinded-independent-review intracranial response rate and duration of intracranial response in VEL-301 patients with measurable brain metastases reach pre-specified precision and follow-up maturity thresholds that support a durability claim?","population":"VEL-301 participants (both arms, approximately 140) with at least one measurable brain metastasis at baseline per RANO-BM, including those with previously treated stable lesions","outcomes":"Intracranial ORR by BICR with exact 95% CI; median duration of intracranial response (Kaplan-Meier, 95% CI) and 6- and 12-month landmark response durability; intracranial PFS; time to CNS progression; number of responders and observed CI widths against pre-specified precision targets","geography":"US + EU5 VEL-301 sites","data_cut":"A CNS-specific data cut at least 6 months after the last responder's first response, taken alongside or shortly after the primary PFS analysis","analysis":"Pre-specified SAP addendum: BICR-based iORR and DoR estimation with CI-width and responder-count targets; Bayesian posterior probability that median DoR exceeds a pre-set clinically meaningful threshold, as a sensitivity analysis; competing-risk handling of death and non-CNS progression; per-arm results shown descriptively","instrument":"RANO-BM criteria applied through blinded independent central review of brain MRI","study_design":"Protocol amendment to the ongoing VEL-301 trial, with a SAP addendum, that (1) adds blinded independent central review of all CNS imaging by RANO-BM, (2) continues scheduled brain MRI after extracranial progression until intracranial progression so DoR is not censored early, and (3) pre-specifies the precision and maturity criteria and the CNS data cut","gap_coverage":"Partial but direct. It does not increase the sample size, but it increases the information per patient (fewer informative censorings), removes investigator-assessment bias, and states up front what precision the sub-study can deliver.","cost_effort":"Low to moderate: imaging vendor scope change, amendment, SAP addendum and extra MRIs at existing sites. No new sites or enrolment.","timing":"Needs an amendment and ethics/regulatory notification, then runs alongside VEL-301 follow-up. Readout is timed to the CNS data cut, which is probably after the 2027-03-31 decision date, so it would feed late-2027 EU5 HTA dossiers and later payer updates.","feasibility_risks":"Amendment approval and site MRI compliance are not yet secured, and no amendment is assumed to be approved. Central review of already-acquired scans must be retroactive and fit within imaging retention. The scheme may be difficult for patients to follow after extracranial progression. Wide CIs may remain if the response rate is lower than expected. Not post-hoc, because it adds prospective data collection on an active study. No new enrolment.","post_hoc":false,"prospective_enrolment":false,"protocol_amendment":true,"start_date":null,"evidence_available":""},"comparative_rationale":"Evidence quality: highest available for the existing 140 patients, because it is randomized-trial data with BICR and prospective follow-up. Cost/effort: lower than adding a new cohort, with no new sites or enrolment. Time: needs an amendment, but readout can follow the primary analysis. Feasibility: depends on amendment approval and imaging logistics. Alternatives considered: (a) a new single-arm CNS cohort (see the second proposal) gives more patients but is slower and costlier; (b) pooling with VEL-201 is already in the library as TAC-024; (c) real-world CNS evidence is already TAC-011; (d) an indirect comparison with competitors does not fix sample precision.","population":"VEL-301 participants (both arms, approximately 140) with at least one measurable brain metastasis at baseline per RANO-BM, including those with previously treated stable lesions","comparator":"VEL-301 randomized comparator arm (osimertinib re-challenge or investigator's choice), shown descriptively; the precision targets apply to the velmaratinib arm","outcomes":"Intracranial ORR by BICR with exact 95% CI; median duration of intracranial response (Kaplan-Meier, 95% CI) and 6- and 12-month landmark response durability; intracranial PFS; time to CNS progression; number of responders and observed CI widths against pre-specified precision targets","data_source":"VEL-301 trial data (prospective brain MRI with blinded independent central review)","study_design":"Protocol amendment to the ongoing VEL-301 trial, with a SAP addendum, that (1) adds blinded independent central review of all CNS imaging by RANO-BM, (2) continues scheduled brain MRI after extracranial progression until intracranial progression so DoR is not censored early, and (3) pre-specifies the precision and maturity criteria and the CNS data cut","duration_months":18,"readout_lag_months":4,"timing_rationale":"Duration covers the amendment, retroactive central review and the extra MRI follow-up until responders have matured to the CNS data cut. The lag covers the BICR reads, database lock for the CNS cut, the SAP-specified analysis and QC of the dossier tables.","withdraw":false,"withdraw_reason":""},{"id":"GAP-020:proposal:2","gap_id":"GAP-020","name":"VEL-CNS: single-arm Phase IIIb confirmatory intracranial cohort after osimertinib","type":"phase3_trial","evidence_question":"In an independent prospective cohort of patients with measurable brain metastases after osimertinib, what are BICR-assessed intracranial ORR and duration of intracranial response with velmaratinib, and are they consistent with the VEL-301 CNS sub-study and VEL-201?","rationale":"Adding a separate prospective cohort of about 100 patients increases the total number of patients with measurable brain metastases by roughly 70%. This directly narrows the CIs on iORR and DoR. It also provides replication for a durability claim that rests on a small sub-study.","proposal_kind":"new","target_tactic_id":null,"expansion_scope":null,"comparative_rationale":"Evidence quality: prospective, protocol-driven imaging with BICR, which is stronger than real-world data (TAC-011) but has no concurrent control, so it supports a durability claim and not comparative superiority. Cost/effort: highest of the options, a new multinational study. Time: slowest, so it will not read out before the 2027-03-31 decision, and an interim can support later HTA updates and re-submissions. Feasibility: moderate, given recruitment competition from osimertinib and NX-441 studies. It is not a duplicate of TAC-010 (a sub-study of VEL-301), TAC-011 (non-interventional) or TAC-024 (a pooled analysis of existing data), because it adds a new prospective cohort. An expansion of TAC-010 is cheaper and faster but cannot add patients without a harder amendment on a randomized trial, so it is offered as the other proposal.","population":"Adults with EGFR-mutant advanced NSCLC progressing after osimertinib, with at least one measurable brain metastasis (≥10 mm) per RANO-BM, ECOG 0-2, approximately 100 patients, with at least 30% aged 65 or over","comparator":"None — single-arm; results benchmarked against the VEL-301 CNS sub-study and VEL-201 intracranial ORR (52%) with pre-specified consistency criteria","outcomes":"Primary: BICR intracranial ORR with exact 95% CI. Key secondary: duration of intracranial response (median, 6- and 12-month landmark), intracranial PFS, time to CNS progression, CNS-directed radiotherapy use, neurocognitive and symptom PRO (EORTC QLQ-BN20), and ILD and QT safety","data_source":"New prospective Phase IIIb study at US and EU5 neuro-oncology and thoracic centres, with central MRI review","study_design":"Open-label, single-arm, multicentre Phase IIIb cohort with BICR RANO-BM, MRI every 8 weeks until intracranial progression, a pre-specified precision target (exact 95% CI half-width), an interim analysis at 12 months, and a pre-specified Bayesian pooled estimate with VEL-301 CNS sub-study and VEL-201 data","duration_months":24,"readout_lag_months":4,"timing_rationale":"About 12 months to enrol 100 patients with measurable brain metastases at selected centres, followed by about 12 months so responders mature enough to estimate median DoR. The lag covers central imaging review, database lock, the analysis and dossier-ready tables.","withdraw":false,"withdraw_reason":""}]}

The expansion adds staged maturity milestones, switching-adjusted OS (RPSFT/IPCW) and a decision rule linking each cut to HTA resubmission. The ITT population and the control arm match VEL-301 (TAC-016). Randomised OS is the only design that fully answers the mature-OS half of the gap. post_hoc=false, prospective_enrolment=false and protocol_amendment=true are all consistent with the design. The amendment is correctly described as not yet approved. Three tightenings: (1) in data_cut, cap the 'or 5 years after last patient randomised' cut so it fits the 54-month duration; (2) fix the switching-adjustment SAP addendum before the Q4 2027 interim OS look, so the adjusted analyses are pre-specified; (3) set start_date once the amendment submission date is known. Mature OS will not exist for the 2027 decisions, so the interim cut and the pre-agreed plan carry that submission.","issues":[],"duplicate_of":null},{"id":"GAP-034:proposal:2","verdict":"revise","confidence":42,"note":"Four problems. (1) Overlap: TAC-020 (natural history after osimertinib recurrence) covers the same population and clinical course, including survival. Either add the OS-tail benchmarking as an expansion of TAC-020, or state clearly what this adds: the extrapolation-validation question. (2) Timing: 8 months build plus 3 months readout is about 11 months. The rationale's claim that it feeds the Jan-Mar 2027 HTA and P&T timelines is not credible. Restate the target as resubmission and the Q4 2027 interim OS. (3) Comparator and validity: a benchmark of real-world standard of care can only validate extrapolation of the VEL-301 control arm. It cannot validate the velmaratinib arm's tail. Say so in outcomes and rationale, and drop the implication that it supports velmaratinib survival projection. (4) Data: 48-month OS in a post-osimertinib second-line cohort has limited follow-up. Name the specific EHR database and EU5 registries, specify the minimum follow-up, and cut 36/48-month landmarks if follow-up is thin. Remove the vague 'recommended OS follow-up schedule' from the study design. A cheaper, faster complement to TAC-015 is reasonable once scoped this way.","issues":["overlap_with_TAC-020","timing","comparator","data_source","rationale"],"duplicate_of":null}]}

calls.reply: {"reviews":[{"id":"GAP-027:proposal:1","verdict":"keep","confidence":72,"note":"The design holds. Frailty-defined PRO cohorts inside the registry give Velmara-specific, longitudinal data with HTA-accepted instruments (QLQ-C30, LC13, EQ-5D-5L), plus utilities for the CEA. An in-registry fit comparator is enough for this gap, which does not require an active comparator. The 12-month recruitment plus 12-month follow-up and 4-month lag are credible. Three points to tighten in the protocol. (1) The registry is only planned, so state that the pre-start amendment is required and unapproved. Do not describe the timeline as firm until the registry start date exists. (2) Frail patients may be a small share of registry enrolment, so set an explicit enrolment cap and quota mechanism for the 150 target. (3) Name one primary endpoint, or specify multiplicity handling for the two co-primaries.","issues":[],"duplicate_of":null},{"id":"GAP-027:proposal:2","verdict":"revise","confidence":40,"note":"The gap needs HTA-grade PRO evidence in frail patients on Velmara. It does not need a comparative design, so the standalone comparison adds cost and confounding without clearly closing the gap better than the registry module. Four fixes. (1) comparator: 'platinum chemotherapy or another EGFR TKI' is too heterogeneous. In frail patients, treatment choice is driven by fitness, so propensity adjustment will not remove confounding by indication, and open-label PRO reporting is also biased. Define one or two named comparator regimens, or drop the active comparator and use frail vs fit. (2) population: the restriction to age 65+, post-osimertinib and frail makes recruiting about 120 Velmara starters per arm in 12 months unrealistic for a newly launched drug. Add a feasibility estimate and a minimum-sample gate. (3) outcomes: the primary at month 6 is vulnerable to death and attrition in frail patients. Specify a composite or joint-modelling strategy. (4) timing: about 32 months to readout, with high cost and separate site set-up. Justify the added cost against the registry expansion, or position this only as a conditional follow-on. Coordinate the frail comparator cohort with TAC-007 to avoid parallel recruitment of the same patients.","issues":["comparator","feasibility","confounding","cost_vs_expansion","timing"],"duplicate_of":null},{"id":"GAP-029:proposal:1","verdict":"revise","confidence":62,"note":"The expansion has valid added scope. TAC-009 has no age 65+ or brain-metastasis strata, TTD, TTNT, OS or IPTW comparison, so this is not a duplicate. Fixes needed. (1) rationale: it says TAC-009 does not specify NX-441 and chemotherapy, but TAC-009's evidence question already names velmaratinib vs NX-441 and chemotherapy. Reframe the added scope as the defined cohorts, strata, outcomes and adjusted analysis. (2) population/data_cut: the cut says 'osimertinib approval in the second-line setting' but the population is progression on first-line osimertinib. Make these consistent. (3) feasibility: velmaratinib starters in the databases may be near zero for a new launch, and NX-441 starters are few. Set numeric minimum cell sizes in the feasibility gate and state that the Velmara comparison may be descriptive or deferred. (4) timing: 6 months of analysis is optimistic when licences and governance across US and EU5 are unconfirmed. Add a data-access lead time, or make the early cut US-only. Retain post_hoc=true, with no amendment needed.","issues":["rationale_overlap","internal_inconsistency","data_access","sample_size","timing"],"duplicate_of":null},{"id":"GAP-029:proposal:2","verdict":"revise","confidence":40,"note":"The gap is about real-world pathways and outcomes after osimertinib. A MAIC answers an efficacy-comparison question (PFS, ORR, iORR) and gives no pathway information, so it cannot close this gap alone. Fixes needed. (1) Reposition it explicitly as a complementary trial-based comparison, or move it to a gap on comparative efficacy. (2) comparator/design: anchoring needs a common comparator, and VEL-301's arms (osimertinib re-challenge or investigator's choice) may not match the NX-441 trial's control arm. Without that link the analysis is unanchored, which is high-bias and weakly accepted by HTA bodies. Confirm the published NX-441 data, including effect modifiers and reported PFS, before committing. (3) data: VEL-301 patient-level data depend on its readout, so the 5-month duration is not credible before 2027 filings. Limit the first phase to VEL-201 single-arm data with clear caveats, and add VEL-301 once available. (4) outcomes: report effective sample size and a pre-specified threshold below which the comparison is not reported.","issues":["gap_mismatch","anchoring","data_availability","timing"],"duplicate_of":null}]}

calls.reply: {"reviews":[{"id":"GAP-001:proposal:1","verdict":"revise","confidence":68,"note":"The US claims design is runnable and fits the gap. It gives observed procedure-level payer costs that the CEA needs. Fix three things. (1) post_hoc is false, but feasibility_risks calls this a post-hoc analysis of existing data. Set post_hoc to true (retrospective analysis of already-collected claims, no prospective enrolment, no amendment) and make the text agree. (2) The recurrence index relies on claims proxies for progression and EGFR status. Name the primary algorithm and the stricter sensitivity definitions in the analysis field, and specify how patients with osimertinib dispensing but no EGFR confirmation are handled. (3) Timing only works if data access and protocol sign-off complete by about end-August 2026, and start_date is null. Set a concrete start_date and a fallback, such as an interim cost table by early November, so the 30 Nov 2026 freeze is not at risk. It is not a duplicate of TAC-006 because it uses different data and methods. Revise the following. (1) Reposition it in the rationale and gap_coverage as a fallback or validation benchmark for the claims analysis, not a stand-alone answer. (2) CMS fee schedules reflect Medicare rates, but the perspective is a US payer perspective that includes commercial payers. Add commercial-to-Medicare multipliers or published commercial cost sources, and ASP-based drug costs. (3) Procedure-frequency data after osimertinib are sparse, so pre-specify how Delphi inputs are weighted and reported, with a transparent evidence grade per input. (4) Two months for a dual-reviewer SLR plus a Delphi panel is tight. Narrow the search scope and pre-register the protocol, or extend duration to about 3 months. There is still margin before the 30 Nov 2026 freeze.","issues":["partial_gap_coverage","payer_perspective_pricing","data_sparsity","duration"],"duplicate_of":null},{"id":"GAP-020:proposal:1","verdict":"revise","confidence":52,"note":"This is a credible, low-cost way to improve the quality of the CNS estimates, but it does not close a gap defined by sample adequacy, because it adds no patients. Revise the following. (1) The population says approximately 140 patients across both arms, but the precision targets apply to the velmaratinib arm. That arm is probably about 70 patients, so the achievable CI widths are much wider than the framing implies. State the per-arm N and the expected CI half-width for plausible iORR and DoR before committing. (2) Central review of already-acquired scans is retroactive, so it is partly post-hoc. Set post_hoc to true, or limit the claim to the prospective components, and say so in feasibility_risks. (3) Continuing MRI after extracranial progression is confounded by subsequent therapy. Pre-specify censoring at new anticancer therapy and estimate the share of patients who have already passed that point. (4) Timing is probably after 2027-03-31. Say explicitly which decisions it can and cannot feed. (5) Pair it with the pooled analysis in TAC-024 so the precision gain is quantified, instead of presenting it as the whole answer.","issues":["sample_size_not_addressed","arm_level_precision","post_hoc_partial","censoring_definition","timing"],"duplicate_of":null},{"id":"GAP-020:proposal:2","verdict":"revise","confidence":40,"note":"A new prospective single-arm cohort would add patients and replication, and it is not a duplicate of TAC-010, TAC-011 or TAC-024. Feasibility and timing are weak as written. (1) Recruiting 100 patients with measurable brain metastases in 12 months is optimistic. Only about 26% of VEL-201 patients had measurable brain metastases (29 of 112), so roughly 400 patients would need to be screened, in competition with osimertinib and NX-441 trials. Add a screening estimate and a site count, and extend enrolment or reduce N. (2) Duration omits study start-up (protocol, ethics, site activation across US and EU5), typically 6 months or more. Revise to about 30 months plus a 4-month lag. (3) The 'Phase IIIb' label and the phase3_trial type do not fit an uncontrolled single-arm cohort. Use Phase IIIb/IV or Phase II, and state whether velmaratinib is already approved. (4) The Bayesian pooling with VEL-301 and VEL-201 needs justification of exchangeability and a pre-specified discount. (5) It will not read out before 2027-03-31, so state which later HTA updates it supports. The 12-month interim is too early to give a median DoR. Consider a smaller cohort inside the planned registry as a cheaper option.","issues":["recruitment_feasibility","duration_startup_omitted","phase_label","timing","pooling_assumptions"],"duplicate_of":null}]}

calls.reply: {"reviews":[{"id":"GAP-021:proposal:1","verdict":"revise","confidence":55,"note":"The scope is valid and not a duplicate of TAC-008, but it needs four fixes. (1) The timing is inconsistent. The design allows 9 months of accrual, 6 months of follow-up and about 4 months of lag, so the first full readout is about 19 months after launch. The timing field says 12-15 months. Correct the timing field, or define an earlier interim cut. (2) Platinum chemotherapy is infused and appears in medical claims, not pharmacy dispensing, so a 60-day dispensing-gap persistence rule does not apply to it. Limit the persistence comparison to oral comparators (NX-441, osimertinib re-challenge). Report chemotherapy separately as time to discontinuation or switch from administration records, or drop it. (3) Claims carry no EGFR status or line of therapy. State a validation plan for the identification algorithm, for example the linked testing subset, and a minimum cohort size for NX-441, which may have low uptake. (4) Confirm that the database has usable Medicare Advantage data and that Medicare FFS and Medicare Advantage can be analysed together. State clearly that the pre-launch benchmark is the only output usable before the 2027-03-31 decision.","issues":["timing_inconsistency","comparator","outcome_definition","data_source_unconfirmed","feasibility"],"duplicate_of":null},{"id":"GAP-021:proposal:2","verdict":"revise","confidence":48,"note":"This is not a duplicate of TAC-008. It uses a different data source and gives an earlier read, so it can stay as a bridge. Four changes are needed. (1) Use the same persistence definition as TAC-008, a 60-day permissible gap, with 45 days as a sensitivity analysis. The current 45-day primary rule undermines the planned alignment check. (2) Address specialty pharmacy leakage. Patients who switch dispensing channels or pharmacies will look like discontinuers, and the feed covers only participating channels. Add a coverage/market-share estimate and a leakage sensitivity analysis. (3) The EGFR-mutant diagnosis and age are often not recorded in dispensing feeds. Add a cohort-definition fallback (Velmara dispense implies the indicated population) and state that the age 65+ cut depends on data availability. (4) The data-sharing agreement is unconfirmed. Name the partner type, and state that linkage to the claims database needs tokenisation and is not assumed. Position it as an interim signal that supports P&T, not as the claims-based answer the gap asks for. Like proposal 1, it cannot report before the 2027-03-31 decision.","issues":["definition_misalignment","data_source_unconfirmed","selection_bias","population_definition","gap_fit"],"duplicate_of":null},{"id":"GAP-023:proposal:1","verdict":"revise","confidence":58,"note":"This is the right design family for the gap, an adjusted external-comparator target trial emulation with bias analyses. It is not a duplicate of TAC-002 or TAC-003. It has five defects. (1) The comparator is single-agent chemotherapy or best supportive care. The VEL-301 control is osimertinib re-challenge or investigator's choice, and regional SoC after osimertinib often includes platinum doublets. Justify the comparator for each region and add platinum-based regimens. Keep BSC as a separate sensitivity cohort, because mixing it in confounds the comparison. (2) The design uses data from the ongoing VEL-301 trial. OS is immature before the Q4 2027 interim, and VEL-301 is a comparison of velmaratinib against active treatment. Specify which data cut, the firewall and the governance. Set protocol_amendment to true, or explain in feasibility_risks why a SAP addendum is not an amendment. The current false/false/false flags understate the governance burden. (3) Trial patients are fit and protocol-monitored, while the real-world SoC patients are not. Add eligibility alignment on ECOG and brain metastases, define time zero, and handle immortal time. Do not compare trial-assessed PFS with rwPFS. Keep OS as the primary outcome. (4) Contracting EHR licences in the US and EU5, building the cohort and analysing the data in 6 months plus 4 months is optimistic. Extend the duration, or define a staged plan with an early feasibility report. (5) Set a minimum effective sample size for the 65+ velmaratinib arm, with a go/no-go if it is not met. The 15 Jan 2027 HTA package will be missed, so say so, and say what the interim feasibility report can support.","issues":["comparator","governance_flags","bias_design","duration","power_feasibility","timeline_vs_decision"],"duplicate_of":null},{"id":"GAP-023:proposal:2","verdict":"revise","confidence":48,"note":"This is a reasonable low-cost fallback and complement to proposal 1. It is a valid expansion of TAC-003 (its added scope is a comparator cohort and more centres), so it is not a duplicate. It needs these changes. (1) Add a minimum velmaratinib-exposed 65+ N and a go/no-go decision point after the interim cut of the two existing centres, because exposure in EU5 around launch may be too small for adjusted HR estimates. (2) A hospital-based comparison of velmaratinib patients against concurrent SoC patients is heavily confounded by indication. Specify the unmeasured-confounding approach (E-values, quantitative bias analysis) and pre-specify the covariates. (3) Overall survival as the primary outcome needs enough follow-up in a retrospective cohort. State a minimum follow-up and the cut-off date. (4) Justify the SoC definition (single-agent chemotherapy or BSC) as above. (5) The protocol amendment, ethics approval and new-centre contracts are each unapproved. Consider a separate comparator-cohort protocol instead of amending a running single-arm review, and keep the TAC-025 publication on its own timeline. State explicitly that there is no US component and that this tactic partly covers the gap and is not powered.","issues":["power_feasibility","confounding","outcome_followup","comparator","amendment_dependency","gap_coverage"],"duplicate_of":null}]}

calls.reply: {"tactics":[{"id":"GAP-029:proposal:1","gap_id":"GAP-029","name":"TAC-009 expansion: NX-441 and platinum-chemotherapy comparator-cohort pathways and outcomes","type":"rwe_study","evidence_question":"After osimertinib failure in EGFR-mutant advanced NSCLC, what treatment pathways and real-world time-to-treatment-discontinuation, time-to-next-treatment and overall survival do patients starting NX-441 or platinum-based chemotherapy experience, and how do these compare descriptively and with adjustment against velmaratinib starters?","rationale":"TAC-009 already asks how treatments are sequenced after osimertinib, including velmaratinib versus NX-441 and chemotherapy. It does not define the NX-441 and platinum-chemotherapy starters as separate outcome cohorts. It also sets no age 65+ or brain-metastasis strata, no TTD, TTNT or OS endpoints, and no adjusted comparison. This child adds those specifications. Its added scope is the defined cohorts, the strata, the outcomes and the adjusted analysis with a feasibility gate. It is not a restatement of the parent's sequencing question.","proposal_kind":"expansion","target_tactic_id":"TAC-009","expansion_scope":{"name":"TAC-009 expansion: NX-441 and platinum-chemotherapy comparator-cohort pathways and outcomes","evidence_question":"After osimertinib failure in EGFR-mutant advanced NSCLC, what treatment pathways and real-world time-to-treatment-discontinuation, time-to-next-treatment and overall survival do patients starting NX-441 or platinum-based chemotherapy experience, and how do these compare descriptively and with adjustment against velmaratinib starters?","population":"Adults with EGFR-mutant advanced NSCLC who progressed on first-line osimertinib and started NX-441 or platinum-based chemotherapy (with or without pemetrexed or immunotherapy) as next line, plus velmaratinib starters where available. Pre-specified strata: age 65 and over, and brain metastases at index.","outcomes":"Line-by-line treatment pathway maps (proportion by next regimen). Real-world time to treatment discontinuation, time to next treatment, real-world progression proxy and overall survival from index. Reasons for discontinuation. It uses an internal non-frail reference instead of a heterogeneous external comparator.","proposal_kind":"expansion","target_tactic_id":"TAC-021","expansion_scope":{"name":"Frailty-stratified HTA-grade PRO module within the Velmara registry","evidence_question":"What are health-related quality of life, symptom and function trajectories over 12 months in frail versus non-frail patients starting Velmara in routine care, measured with HTA-grade instruments?","population":"Registry patients with EGFR-mutant advanced NSCLC progressing after osimertinib who start Velmara, with frailty assessed at baseline by G8 and Clinical Frailty Scale. Frail patients (G8 of 14 or lower confirmed by CFS 5 or above, or ECOG PS 2) are oversampled to a target of about 100, with non-frail registry patients as the internal reference, at US and EU5 registry sites.","outcomes":"Primary: time to definitive deterioration, defined as a decline of 10 points or more in EORTC QLQ-C30 global health status/QoL or death, over 6 months. It includes a composite deterioration-or-death primary estimand, joint modelling of longitudinal PRO and survival, mixed models for repeated measures, a minimal important difference for responder analyses, covariate-adjusted frail versus non-frail comparison, and missing-not-at-random sensitivity analyses. Mapping of EQ-5D-5L to utilities is by country-specific value sets.","instrument":"EORTC QLQ-C30, EORTC QLQ-LC13, EQ-5D-5L, PRO-CTCAE, Zarit Burden Interview short form, G8, Clinical Frailty Scale","study_design":"Prospective, non-interventional PRO module nested in the planned TAC-021 registry. The internal frail versus non-frail comparison is confounded and is not a treatment-effect comparison. Prospective enrolment is required, and the study is not post hoc.","post_hoc":false,"prospective_enrolment":true,"protocol_amendment":true,"start_date":null,"evidence_available":""},"comparative_rationale":"Versus a new standalone frail cohort (GAP-027:proposal:2): the registry module is cheaper, reuses sites, ethics and data infrastructure, and starts sooner because it needs only an amendment. Versus extending the TAC-013 survey: a survey is the cheapest and fastest but is cross-sectional, not Velmara-specific, and unlikely to be accepted by HTA bodies. The final readout is after the 2027-03-31 decision."},{"id":"GAP-027:proposal:2","gap_id":"GAP-027","name":"Conditional frail-patient PRO cohort with named comparator regimen in 2L EGFR-mutant NSCLC","type":"pro_study","evidence_question":"How do health-related quality of life and time to deterioration over 6 to 12 months in frail patients with EGFR-mutant NSCLC starting Velmara compare, as supportive evidence, with frail patients starting carboplatin-pemetrexed?","rationale":"If the registry module cannot recruit enough frail patients, or HTA bodies ask for comparative frail PRO evidence, a dedicated cohort gives controlled frail recruitment and validated PRO collection. It is revised to answer the objection: the comparator is a single named regimen, the primary estimand handles death and attrition, a feasibility estimate and minimum-sample gate are added, and the study is positioned as a conditional follow-on coordinated with TAC-007.","proposal_kind":"new","target_tactic_id":null,"expansion_scope":null,"comparative_rationale":"Versus the registry module (GAP-027:proposal:1): this study has higher evidence quality for a comparative question because recruitment, comparator and timing of PRO collection are controlled. It costs substantially more, needs separate site set-up, ethics and contracting, and reads out later. For these reasons it is a conditional follow-on, triggered only if the registry module misses the month-9 minimum-sample gate or an HTA body requests a comparative frail estimate. Its comparison is still observational and open-label, so it is labelled supportive. It does not duplicate TAC-007 (clinical effectiveness), TAC-003 (single-arm chart review) or TAC-013 (non-Velmara-specific survey).","population":"Adults aged 65 and over with EGFR-mutant advanced NSCLC progressing after osimertinib who are frail (G8 of 14 or lower confirmed by CFS 5 or above, or ECOG PS 2), starting Velmara or carboplatin-pemetrexed as second-line therapy at US and EU5 oncology centres. Target about 100 Velmara and about 60 comparator patients, with a minimum gate of 60 Velmara patients. Feasibility is to be confirmed by a site-level census before activation; the frail share of eligible post-osimertinib patients and Velmara uptake are assumptions that need verification. Exclusions: PRO completion not feasible even with caregiver support, and concurrent trial participation.","comparator":"Carboplatin-pemetrexed as a single named regimen, in sites where it is routine second-line therapy for frail patients. Comparison is supportive and prespecified as exploratory, with overlap weighting on baseline fitness, frailty and performance status, E-values, and acknowledgement of residual confounding by indication and open-label reporting bias. Within-Velmara frail results are the primary evidence.","outcomes":"Primary: time to definitive deterioration, defined as a decline of 10 points or more in EORTC QLQ-C30 global health status/QoL or death, over 6 months (composite estimand, with a joint model of longitudinal PRO and survival as sensitivity analysis). Secondary: QLQ-C30 and QLQ-LC13 trajectories to month 12, EQ-5D-5L utilities by treatment and progression state, PRO-CTCAE, Zarit short form caregiver burden, discontinuation, unplanned hospitalisations and ED visits, and G8/CFS trajectory.","data_source":"Prospective primary data collection at US and EU5 oncology centres: ePRO at baseline and months 1, 3, 6, 9 and 12, clinician-assessed frailty, and medical records for treatment and clinical events. It uses a composite deterioration-or-death primary estimand, joint modelling, mixed models for repeated measures, and missing-not-at-random sensitivity analyses. A minimum-sample gate applies at month 9: if fewer than 40 Velmara frail patients are enrolled, the study stops and reports the registry module only. Coordination with TAC-007: shared frailty definition and sites, with consent so TAC-007 frail patients can be invited into PRO collection, without double enrolment or parallel recruitment of the same patients.","duration_months":30,"readout_lag_months":5,"timing_rationale":"About 3 months for site selection, ethics and contracting, about 15 months to recruit with a frail Velmara-start population that is small at launch, and 12 months of follow-up for the last patient give 30 months. A 6-month primary analysis can be read out earlier, around month 24 plus lag. A readout lag of about 5 months covers PRO scoring, overlap weighting, joint models and HTA-format reporting. The study will not support the 2027-03-31 decision and is aimed at resubmissions and later payer updates."}]}

Feasibility: moderate, since access to EU5 registries is not confirmed and follow-up in a post-osimertinib cohort is limited, so long landmarks are cut. Compared with a stand-alone new RWE study, the expansion avoids duplicating the TAC-020 population. Compared with expanding TAC-015 (GAP-034:proposal:1), which yields velmaratinib OS but only after 2029, this is a cheaper, faster complement and not a substitute.","population":"Adults with advanced EGFR-mutant NSCLC who progressed on first-line osimertinib and started subsequent systemic therapy (platinum chemotherapy, chemo-immunotherapy or other regional standard of care), with VEL-301 eligibility criteria applied as far as the data allow; patients must have at least 12 months of potential follow-up from the start of subsequent therapy","comparator":"Real-world standard of care after osimertinib compared with the VEL-301 control arm (extrapolation validation only); no velmaratinib comparison","outcomes":"OS from start of subsequent therapy (median; 12- and 24-month survival; 36-month survival only if at least 30 patients remain at risk at 36 months; no 48-month landmark); shape of the hazard function over time; follow-up completeness and median follow-up; fit and external validation of parametric and flexible extrapolations of the VEL-301 control-arm OS against the observed benchmark. Validation applies to the control-arm tail only and does not validate the velmaratinib arm's tail.","data_source":"US: Flatiron Health EHR-derived de-identified database. calls.reply: {"tactics":[{"id":"GAP-023:proposal:1","gap_id":"GAP-023","name":"Target trial emulation of velmaratinib versus regional active SoC in patients aged 65+ using VEL-201/VEL-301 IPD and US/EU5 real-world comparator","type":"rwe_study","evidence_question":"After adjustment for baseline confounding and alignment of eligibility, how does overall survival with velmaratinib compare with regional active standard of care (platinum-based doublet or single-agent chemotherapy) in patients aged 65 and over with EGFR-mutant NSCLC progressing on osimertinib, with best supportive care as a separate sensitivity cohort?","rationale":"Payers and HTA bodies said the VEL-301 elderly subgroup (TAC-002) is only descriptive and that no adjusted comparison against regional SoC exists. TAC-003 is single-arm. TAC-007 holds this question as a placeholder with no design. This tactic specifies a staged target trial emulation with a prespecified protocol, explicit comparator justification, eligibility alignment, defined time zero, minimum-sample go/no-go rules and bias quantification, so HTA reviewers can critique it. It is staged so that it starts with the completed VEL-201 data and adds ongoing VEL-301 data only under governance and only when OS is mature enough.","proposal_kind":"expansion","target_tactic_id":"TAC-007","expansion_scope":{"name":"Target trial emulation of velmaratinib versus regional active SoC in patients aged 65+ using VEL-201/VEL-301 IPD and US/EU5 real-world comparator","evidence_question":"After adjustment for baseline confounding and alignment of eligibility, how does overall survival with velmaratinib compare with regional active standard of care (platinum-based doublet or single-agent chemotherapy) in patients aged 65 and over with EGFR-mutant NSCLC progressing on osimertinib, with best supportive care as a separate sensitivity cohort?","population":"Adults aged 65 years and over with EGFR-mutant advanced NSCLC and documented progression on prior osimertinib, with real-world eligibility aligned to VEL-201/VEL-301 criteria (ECOG 0-1 in the primary analysis, ECOG 2 as a sensitivity analysis; brain metastases status recorded and stratified; adequate organ function). Velmaratinib arm: VEL-201 participants aged 65+ (completed Phase II) and, subject to firewalled governance and OS maturity, velmaratinib-arm VEL-301 participants aged 65+. Comparator arm: patients aged 65+ meeting the same aligned eligibility at the start of their first post-osimertinib line in US and EU5 routine care who received regional active SoC (platinum-based doublet chemotherapy, or single-agent chemotherapy for platinum-ineligible patients). Patients receiving best supportive care only form a separate sensitivity cohort and are not pooled with the active SoC comparator.","outcomes":"Primary: overall survival from time zero (treatment initiation of the first post-osimertinib line; first dose for trial patients), reported as adjusted hazard ratio with 95% CI. Secondary: time to treatment discontinuation or death, defined identically in trial and real-world data. Real-world PFS is described within the real-world cohort only and is not compared with trial-assessed PFS. Exploratory: hospitalisation rate in real-world data. Sensitivity: BSC-only cohort comparison, ECOG 2 inclusion, E-values and quantitative bias analysis.","geography":"US and EU5 (France, Germany, Italy, Spain, UK), reported by region for HTA","data_cut":"Stage A: VEL-201 final dataset (completed trial) plus the latest refresh of licensed real-world data. Stage B: VEL-301 velmaratinib-arm 65+ data added at the earliest of the primary PFS database lock or the Q4 2027 interim OS cut, only if the OS maturity rule is met (median follow-up of at least 12 months in the 65+ velmaratinib patients). Exact cut dates to be set in the protocol, with no data access assumed approved.","analysis":"Protocol and SAP finalised before any outcome analysis, based on a target trial specification (eligibility, treatment strategies, time zero, follow-up, causal contrast). Comparator rationale: regional guideline review and HTA/KOL confirmation to define the active SoC list per country, with platinum doublets as the primary comparator because they are widely used after osimertinib in patients fit enough, single-agent chemotherapy as a stratum for platinum-ineligible patients, and BSC kept as a separate sensitivity cohort because pooling it would confound the comparison. Eligibility alignment: apply the trial criteria on ECOG, brain metastases, organ function and prior osimertinib to real-world patients. Time zero is treatment initiation in both sources. Real-world eligibility is assessed in a window before treatment start. Immortal time from trial screening is handled by a landmark sensitivity analysis and a clone-censor-weight sensitivity analysis. Overlap or inverse-probability-of-treatment weighting on prespecified confounders (age, ECOG, comorbidity, brain metastases, prior lines, time on osimertinib, EGFR subtype, region). Balance diagnostics, region-stratified analyses, negative-control outcomes, E-values and quantitative bias analysis. Go/no-go: proceed to the adjusted comparison only if at least 60 velmaratinib-treated patients aged 65+ are available, the weighted effective sample size is at least 50 per arm and at least 40 OS events are expected. Otherwise the output is a descriptive feasibility and balance report and no adjusted HR is reported (thresholds to be confirmed by the statistician).","instrument":"","study_design":"Staged hybrid external-comparator cohort study using a target trial emulation framework. Stage 0 (feasibility report): counts of eligible velmaratinib and real-world SoC patients, covariate overlap and the go/no-go rule. Stage A: individual patient data from velmaratinib-treated patients aged 65+ in the completed VEL-201 study are compared with a contemporaneous real-world SoC cohort from de-identified oncology EHR databases. Stage B: velmaratinib-arm 65+ data from ongoing VEL-301 are added under a firewall (independent statistics team, no access for the VEL-301 study team, DMC and sponsor governance sign-off) once the OS maturity rule is met.","gap_coverage":"Directly closes the gap: gives an adjusted comparison versus regional active SoC in patients aged 65+ for both US and EU5, distinct from the descriptive VEL-301 elderly subgroup (TAC-002) and the single-arm chart review (TAC-003). Power is limited by the number of velmaratinib-treated elderly patients, and the output is observational, not a powered randomised comparison.","cost_effort":"Moderate to high: licensing real-world data in the US and EU5, trial IPD access and governance, statistical programming, eligibility alignment and bias analyses. Cheaper and faster than a new prospective comparative study. More expensive than the chart-review companion cohort.","timing":"About 3 months to contract data and produce the Stage 0 feasibility report, about 12 months in total to last data in (cohort build, Stage A, then Stage B when the maturity rule is met), then about 4 months to a reviewed readout. The 15 January 2027 HTA elderly package will be missed. The Stage 0 feasibility report, with the protocol, comparator justification and sample counts, can support HTA clarification responses and credibility discussions, and the final result is aimed at later HTA submissions and a US P&T update. calls.reply: {"tactics":[{"id":"GAP-021:proposal:1","gap_id":"GAP-021","name":"TAC-008 expansion: US claims persistence with oral comparator benchmarks, separate chemotherapy discontinuation reporting and Medicare 65+ stratification","type":"rwe_study","evidence_question":"How do six-month persistence and discontinuation for Velmara compare with those of oral comparators (NX-441 and osimertinib re-challenge) after osimertinib failure in US claims, overall and in patients aged 65 and over, and how does time to discontinuation or switch on platinum chemotherapy compare descriptively?","rationale":"Payers distrust trial persistence and want routine-care persistence. This revision limits the dispensing-gap persistence rule to oral products, adds an algorithm validation plan and a minimum cohort size, and corrects the timing.","proposal_kind":"expansion","target_tactic_id":"TAC-008","expansion_scope":{"name":"TAC-008 expansion: US claims persistence with oral comparator benchmarks, separate chemotherapy discontinuation reporting and Medicare 65+ stratification","evidence_question":"How do six-month persistence and discontinuation for Velmara compare with those of oral comparators (NX-441 and osimertinib re-challenge) after osimertinib failure in US claims, overall and in patients aged 65 and over, and how does time to discontinuation or switch on platinum chemotherapy compare descriptively?","population":"Adults with EGFR-mutant advanced NSCLC who start a new line of therapy after osimertinib in US claims. Velmara initiators form the index cohort. New initiators of the oral comparators NX-441 and osimertinib re-challenge form the persistence benchmark cohorts. New initiators of platinum chemotherapy form a separate descriptive cohort. Patients aged 65 and over (Medicare Advantage and FFS) form a pre-specified stratum.","outcomes":"Primary: proportion persistent at 6 months with a 60-day permissible gap in the oral cohorts (Velmara, NX-441, osimertinib re-challenge). Secondary: time to discontinuation or switch (Kaplan-Meier) in all cohorts, with chemotherapy measured from medical-claims administration records, proportion of days covered in the oral cohorts, discontinuation and switching patterns, and the same measures in the 65+ stratum.","geography":"US","data_cut":"Pre-launch cut: oral and chemotherapy benchmark cohorts from existing claims history, before launch. Interim post-launch cut: Velmara initiators from the first 3 months after launch, once they have 6 months of follow-up and claims run-out, about 13 months after launch. First full cut: all initiators from the first 9 months after launch, about 19 months after launch. Refreshed every 6 months thereafter.","analysis":"Propensity-score/IPTW adjustment for age, sex, comorbidity, prior therapy, brain metastases proxy and payer type. Algorithm sensitivity analyses on stricter and looser EGFR and line-of-therapy definitions.","instrument":"","study_design":"Retrospective, new-user, active-comparator cohort study in a US longitudinal pharmacy and medical claims database, with an index date at first dispense or first administration and at least 6 months of follow-up. Persistence with a 60-day permissible gap is assessed in oral cohorts only (Velmara, NX-441, osimertinib re-challenge) from pharmacy dispensing records. Platinum chemotherapy is infused, so it is reported separately and descriptively as time to discontinuation or switch from medical-claims administration records, with no persistence-gap comparison. Lung cancer, EGFR status and line of therapy are identified by algorithm, validated against a linked testing-record subset (target positive predictive value of at least 80 percent). A minimum of 100 evaluable initiators with 6 months of follow-up is required for any adjusted NX-441 comparison, otherwise NX-441 is reported descriptively. The 65+ stratum is a pre-specified subgroup. Medicare Advantage and FFS are analysed together only if the database shows usable capture of both, otherwise they are stratified.","gap_coverage":"Covers the payer ask for claims-based six-month persistence and discontinuation. Adds oral comparative context, a descriptive chemotherapy view and an elderly stratum that Velmara-only reporting would lack.","cost_effort":"Moderate incremental cost over the parent: extra cohort build, algorithm validation, confounding adjustment and statistical analysis, with no new data purchase beyond the licence the parent already needs. Much lower than a prospective study.","timing":"Only the pre-launch comparator benchmark can be ready before the 2027-03-31 decision. Velmara 6-month persistence cannot be reported before then, because Velmara claims only start accruing at the 2027-H1 launch. The interim cut (first 3 months of initiators) is expected about 13 months after launch (3 months accrual, 6 months follow-up, about 4 months run-out and analysis). The first full cut is expected about 19 months after launch (9 months accrual, 6 months follow-up, about 4 months lag).","feasibility_risks":"Few Velmara patients early after launch gives imprecise estimates, and the 65+ stratum will be smaller still. Claims run-out lags delay each cut. Whether the database has usable Medicare Advantage data, and whether FFS and Advantage can be pooled, is not yet confirmed. This is a secondary-data study, so there is no enrolment, no trial amendment and no post-hoc trial analysis. The parent protocol is still proposed and the added scope must be written into it. Database access and licensing are not yet confirmed.","post_hoc":false,"prospective_enrolment":false,"protocol_amendment":false,"start_date":null,"evidence_available":null},"comparative_rationale":"Expansion versus a new standalone study. It is a descriptive retrospective US claims analysis, which gives the observed procedure-level payer costs the CEA needs, with outputs shaped as unit costs by health state. Strengths: the recurrence proxy has pre-specified sensitivity definitions (S1-S3), EGFR-unconfirmed patients form their own stratum with a 10% rule for choosing the base case, and cost estimation is censoring-adjusted. As an expansion of TAC-006 it adds valid scope (population, data source, design), so it is not a duplicate. Three points to tighten. (1) The data licence is not secured, so make the 2026-08-14 access checkpoint an explicit go/no-go owned by a named person. (2) The population is osimertinib-only, so align the evidence_question wording ('third-generation EGFR TKI') with it. (3) Systemic-therapy drug costs after recurrence must not double-count the treatment costs the CEA models for each arm. The 3-month build plus 1-month readout is tight but credible for a licensed database already in hand.","issues":[],"duplicate_of":null},{"id":"GAP-001:proposal:2","verdict":"keep","confidence":63,"note":"Holds as a fallback, benchmark and EU5 input source, not as a stand-alone answer. The gap asks for routine-practice costs and this is modelled micro-costing, so keep it positioned that way. It is cheap, uses public sources, and is distinct from the claims study. The pre-registered protocol, evidence grading (A-D), Delphi agreement thresholds and the 25% cross-check against claims are good practice. Two cautions. (1) Evidence grade A is defined as observed US claims or registry data, which becomes circular once TAC-006 results arrive, so keep the grading independent of the claims output. (2) Published procedure frequencies after osimertinib are sparse, so expect many C/D inputs and widen the PSA ranges. Add an explicit trigger: activate as the CEA base case only if claims access is not executed by 2026-08-14.","issues":[],"duplicate_of":null},{"id":"GAP-020:proposal:1","verdict":"revise","confidence":58,"note":"Valid expansion of TAC-010: BICR, extended MRI and a pre-specified SAP add real scope, and the post_hoc/amendment flags are correctly set. But the precision targets are never defined. analysis gives only planning half-widths (about ±11-12 points for iORR, ±3.5-4 months for DoR), while outcomes refer to 'pre-specified targets'. Fix: state numeric adequacy thresholds in the SAP addendum, for example a lower 95% CI bound for iORR and a minimum median DoR lower bound, agreed with payer/HTA input, so the tactic can say whether the gap is closed. Also (1) the precision-gain table depends on TAC-024, which is only proposed, so sequence it or make it optional; (2) acknowledge that mixing BICR (VEL-301) with investigator-assessed VEL-201 data weakens the pooling; (3) retroactive BICR on already-acquired scans must be confirmed against imaging retention, and MRI after extracranial progression is confounded by later therapy (the censoring rules mitigate this). It adds no patients, so it only partly answers the adequacy gap and cannot meet the 2026-11-30 or 2027-03-31 deadlines. That is acceptable as the low-cost first step.","issues":["precision_targets_undefined","dependency_on_proposed_tactic","partial_gap_coverage","timing"],"duplicate_of":null},{"id":"GAP-020:proposal:2","verdict":"revise","confidence":48,"note":"Runnable in principle, but it is the costliest and slowest option with a modest payoff. calls.reply: {"reviews":[{"id":"GAP-021:proposal:1","verdict":"keep","confidence":74,"note":"Sound expansion of TAC-008. It adds scope the parent lacks: oral comparator benchmarks, a separate descriptive chemotherapy view and a 65+ stratum. The persistence gap rule is correctly limited to oral products, and chemotherapy is reported as time to discontinuation or switch from medical claims. Algorithm validation (PPV target of at least 80%), a minimum of 100 initiators for adjusted NX-441 comparison, and the dated interim and full cuts (13 and 19 months post-launch) are credible. It is a secondary-data study with no enrolment, amendment or post-hoc trial analysis. It is honest that Velmara persistence cannot be read out before 2027-03-31. Watch items: osimertinib re-challenge is an unusual post-osimertinib option, so confirm that cohort is large enough to be a meaningful benchmark. Confirm Medicare Advantage/FFS capture and database licensing before relying on the 65+ stratum.","issues":[],"duplicate_of":null},{"id":"GAP-021:proposal:2","verdict":"revise","confidence":52,"note":"A faster bridge is useful, but the outcomes and framing need changes. (1) outcomes: a 3-month persistence readout with a 60-day permissible gap is nearly uninformative, because a patient must miss 60 of the first 90 days to count as discontinued. Use a shorter gap (30 days) or time to first missed refill for the 3-month interim cut, and keep the 60-day gap for the 6-month cut. (2) gap fit: the gap asks for claims-based persistence, and this feed is not claims. Relabel it explicitly as an interim bridge that must not be presented to P&T as the claims-based answer. This also keeps it from overlapping TAC-008 on the same evidence question and population. (3) data_source: the partner is unidentified. Add a named-partner shortlist, a go/no-go on feed coverage (share of Velmara dispensing captured), and a fallback if coverage is too low. (4) Linkage to claims is not assumed, so aggregate-level alignment should be stated as the default, not the aspiration. Specify the readout schedule, which is about 5 months post-launch for the 3-month cut.","issues":["outcome_definition","gap_fit","data_source","duplicate_risk"],"duplicate_of":null},{"id":"GAP-023:proposal:1","verdict":"revise","confidence":64,"note":"Strongest design for the gap: a staged target trial emulation with eligibility alignment, time-zero and immortal-time handling, a go/no-go, bias quantification and honest scope (not powered, misses the 15 Jan 2027 and 31 Mar 2027 dates). The flags (post_hoc true, amendment true, no enrolment, nothing assumed approved) are consistent. One change is needed. outcomes/data_source: overall survival is the primary outcome, but EHR-derived databases (especially in EU5) under-capture deaths, which biases the real-world arm towards longer survival. Add linkage to mortality sources (for example US composite or national death records, and country death registries in EU5), with a minimum death-capture sensitivity requirement, or restrict the real-world arm to sources with validated mortality. Also state in the SAP how VEL-201 (single-arm Phase II) and VEL-301 velmaratinib-arm patients are pooled, including a heterogeneity check by study. Keep the biostatistics confirmation of the go/no-go thresholds.","issues":["outcome_ascertainment","data_source","pooling_heterogeneity"],"duplicate_of":null},{"id":"GAP-023:proposal:2","verdict":"keep","confidence":58,"note":"A credible lower-cost, partial complement to proposal 1. It adds a concurrent comparator cohort to the TAC-003 network under a separate linked protocol, so the running single-arm review and TAC-025 are not delayed. It is retrospective with no enrolment and no post-hoc trial data. The amendment flag is true and no approval is assumed. The 11-month duration and 4-month lag are consistent with ethics, abstraction and the minimum 6-month follow-up. The scope is acknowledged to be EU5-only, observational and not powered. Tighten before protocol: the go/no-go is based only on the number of velmaratinib patients (at least 30). Add a minimum expected-events criterion (for example at least 40-60 OS events overall), since 30 exposed patients may give very wide hazard ratio intervals. Plan for strong confounding by indication, because velmaratinib patients may differ in fitness from chemotherapy patients at the same centres. Also confirm that enough velmaratinib-treated elderly patients exist in EU5 before launch.","issues":[],"duplicate_of":null}]}
