calls.reply: {"tactics":[{"id":"GAP-029:proposal:2","gap_id":"GAP-029","name":"VEL-201 unanchored MAIC versus published NX-441 and platinum-chemotherapy trial arms after osimertinib (supportive efficacy context)","type":"maic","evidence_question":"After matching on available prognostic and effect-modifying characteristics, how do velmaratinib's ORR, duration of response and, if feasible, intracranial ORR in VEL-201 compare with published aggregate trial results for NX-441 and for platinum-based chemotherapy after osimertinib?","rationale":"This is supportive, trial-based efficacy context only. It does not close GAP-029, which concerns real-world pathways and outcomes after NX-441 or chemotherapy. That gap stays with the TAC-009 real-world sequencing study. This tactic places Velmara's efficacy beside both comparators while the real-world work matures. It uses completed VEL-201 patient-level data (112 patients, published 2025), so it does not wait for the VEL-301 readout. The output is unanchored, high-bias and not HTA-grade. It should be presented as supportive context and not as comparative proof. Real-world chemotherapy cohorts are kept out of the matching and appear only as separate descriptive context.","proposal_kind":"new","target_tactic_id":null,"expansion_scope":null,"comparative_rationale":"New vs expansion: no accepted tactic covers an indirect comparison. TAC-009 is a real-world sequencing study and TAC-004 is a CEA. Folding a MAIC into TAC-009 would mix incompatible methods and data sources, so a separate tactic is cleaner. Evidence quality: lower than an adjusted real-world comparison, because VEL-201 is single-arm, no common comparator exists and the analysis is unanchored, so residual confounding is high and HTA acceptance is weak. Cost and effort: lowest of the options, about 5 months of analyst and literature-review time and no new data collection. Time: it can deliver supportive material before the 2027 filings. Feasibility: conditional on a go/no-go gate after the literature review. The gate checks that published NX-441 and chemotherapy trial reports give enough effect modifiers and that the post-weighting effective sample size (ESS) stays above threshold. The 29-patient CNS subset is likely to fail the ESS gate, so intracranial results will probably be descriptive only. It complements the TAC-009 expansion and does not replace it.","population":"Adults with EGFR-mutant advanced NSCLC progressing after osimertinib. Index population: VEL-201 Phase II patients with patient-level data (n=112), including the 29 with measurable brain metastases for the conditional intracranial analysis. Comparator populations: published aggregate trial populations for NX-441 and for platinum-based chemotherapy after osimertinib. VEL-301 patients are not included in this tactic.","comparator":"NX-441 and platinum-based chemotherapy, each from published aggregate trial data only (trial arms). The analysis is unanchored because VEL-201 is single-arm and no common comparator is expected. Published real-world chemotherapy cohorts are not matched or pooled with trial arms. They are summarised separately as descriptive context only.","outcomes":"Primary: ORR and duration of response, the endpoints reported for VEL-201. Conditional: intracranial ORR, reported only if the 29-patient subset passes the ESS gate, otherwise shown as unweighted descriptive data. PFS is included only if patient-level VEL-201 PFS is confirmed and comparator PFS definitions are compatible. Supporting outputs: effective sample size after weighting, covariate balance, sensitivity to the matching variables, and quantitative bias analysis. Pre-specified no-report rule: an ESS below about 50% of the original sample, or fewer than 3 matchable prognostic covariates, means the comparison is not reported for that comparator or outcome.","data_source":"Existing VEL-201 Phase II patient-level data (completed trial, post-hoc use only, with data access to be confirmed by the study owner). Published NX-441 and platinum-chemotherapy trial aggregate data identified through a targeted literature review. Published real-world chemotherapy cohorts are used only for separate descriptive context.","study_design":"Step 1, targeted literature review (about 2 months): identify NX-441 and platinum-chemotherapy trial publications after osimertinib, extract outcomes, definitions and baseline characteristics (ECOG, age, brain metastases, prior lines, EGFR mutation type), and tabulate real-world chemotherapy cohorts separately. Step 2, go/no-go gate: proceed for a given comparator only if its publications report enough effect modifiers and a feasibility check shows the ESS would stay above the pre-specified threshold. Otherwise stop for that comparator and deliver a descriptive feasibility report. Step 3, pre-specified SAP and unanchored MAIC of VEL-201 against each trial comparator separately, with propensity-type weighting on the selected covariates, ESS and balance reporting, quantitative bias analysis and sensitivity analyses. Step 4, report the output explicitly labelled unanchored, high-bias and not HTA-grade supportive context, with the real-world chemotherapy cohorts as a separate descriptive table. Any VEL-301 update would be a separate later decision after its readout.","duration_months":5,"readout_lag_months":2,"timing_rationale":"The targeted review, comparator data extraction and go/no-go gate take about 2 months. Weighting, sensitivity and bias analyses for comparators that pass the gate take about 3 months. VEL-201 data are complete, so there is no data-readout dependency, although data access and a SAP must be agreed up front. The 2-month readout lag covers statistical QC, independent methodological review, and writing the report with the required caveats. If the gate fails for a comparator, that comparator drops out and the timeline shortens."}]}

calls.reply: {"tactics":[{"id":"GAP-034:proposal:1","gap_id":"GAP-034","name":"VEL-301 extended survival follow-up with pre-specified OS maturity milestones and crossover-adjusted analyses","type":"long_term_followup","evidence_question":"What is the overall survival of velmaratinib versus osimertinib re-challenge or investigator's choice in VEL-301 at pre-specified maturity milestones, after adjustment for treatment switching where subsequent-therapy data allow, and what follow-up plan applies if OS is immature at each milestone?","rationale":"Payers and HTA bodies will see immature OS at the 2027 decisions. Any later cut would need a further amendment and is not assumed.","analysis":"Stratified log-rank and Cox HR in ITT; RMST differences; RPSFT and IPCW sensitivity analyses for crossover and subsequent therapy. If crossover or subsequent therapy cannot be captured adequately, switching adjustment is limited to a pre-specified sensitivity analysis and this is stated in the SAP addendum. Landmarks are limited to what follow-up supports for late enrollers, using the enrolment-completion date once confirmed.","instrument":"","study_design":"Protocol amendment to the ongoing randomised VEL-301 Phase III to extend long-term survival follow-up (visits or registry or vital-status tracing every 3-6 months after progression), add structured subsequent-therapy and crossover capture, add the staged OS maturity milestones, and add a statistical analysis plan addendum for switching-adjusted OS","gap_coverage":"Addresses both parts of the gap: randomised OS data at staged maturity and an explicit follow-up plan where OS is immature. Whether VEL-301 permits or records crossover and subsequent therapy is not confirmed and must be checked against the protocol. Without this data RPSFT/IPCW cannot be run. The final cut depends on event accrual and on the enrolment-completion date. This is not a post-hoc analysis because follow-up is prospective on an ongoing study. No new enrolment is required, so prospective_enrolment is false. protocol_amendment is true.","post_hoc":false,"prospective_enrolment":false,"protocol_amendment":true,"start_date":null,"evidence_available":null},"comparative_rationale":"Evidence quality: highest, because it gives randomised, protocol-specified OS versus the active comparator. Cost/effort: moderate, because it extends an existing trial and avoids a new study. A new external-control study would cost similar money but give only observational data. Time: slowest for mature data (about 4.5 years from the amendment, with usable later cuts about 2029-2031). Only the investigator's-choice portion of the control arm is comparable, because osimertinib re-challenge patients are rare in routine care and are excluded from the comparison. Comparing extrapolations with the immature Q4 2027 control-arm OS is a weak validation, and results will be reported as such.","instrument":"","study_design":"Retrospective cohort study within the TAC-020 population using existing data. If it slips, the fallback is a stand-alone cohort build with the same eligibility and sources, at the cost of some extra time and effort and without sharing the TAC-020 cohort work. The comparison is a weak, descriptive check of the control-arm tail only and does not validate the velmaratinib arm's tail.","data_source":"Primary: Flatiron Health EHR-derived de-identified database (US), CRISP registry (Germany), ESME advanced NSCLC database (France), UK NCRAS/SACT data. calls.reply: {"tactics":[{"id":"GAP-027:proposal:1","gap_id":"GAP-027","name":"Frail-patient HTA-grade PRO module within the prospective Velmara registry","type":"registry","evidence_question":"What are the health-related quality of life trajectories and time to definitive deterioration over 6 to 12 months in frail patients starting Velmara in routine care, collected with HTA-grade instruments?","rationale":"The registry (TAC-021) already plans prospective collection of patient-reported outcomes in Velmara starters but does not target or define frail patients. A frailty-stratified, HTA-grade PRO module adds frail-specific Velmara PRO evidence at the lowest incremental cost, using existing site infrastructure, consent and data capture.","proposal_kind":"expansion","target_tactic_id":"TAC-021","expansion_scope":{"name":"Frail-patient HTA-grade PRO module within the prospective Velmara registry","evidence_question":"What are the health-related quality of life trajectories and time to definitive deterioration over 6 to 12 months in frail patients starting Velmara in routine care, collected with HTA-grade instruments?","population":"Adults with EGFR-mutant advanced NSCLC starting Velmara as second-line therapy after osimertinib in registry sites in the US and EU5 who are frail, defined as G8 of 14 or lower confirmed by Clinical Frailty Scale 5 or above, or ECOG PS 2. Age is not restricted. Patients aged 65 and over are a prespecified subgroup. Target about 100 frail patients, with enrichment by site-level frailty screening at registry enrolment. Excluded: patients unable to complete PROs even with caregiver support.","outcomes":"Primary: time to definitive deterioration, defined as a decline of 10 points or more in EORTC QLQ-C30 global health status/QoL or death, over 6 months. Secondary: QLQ-C30 and QLQ-LC13 trajectories to month 12, EQ-5D-5L utilities by progression state, PRO-CTCAE, Zarit short form caregiver burden, treatment discontinuation, unplanned hospitalisations and ED visits, and G8/CFS trajectory. Frail versus non-frail Velmara registry patients are compared descriptively.","geography":"US and EU5 registry sites","data_cut":"Interim descriptive cut when the first 40 frail patients reach 6 months; primary cut when the last frail patient reaches 6 months; final cut at 12 months of follow-up.","analysis":"Time to definitive deterioration or death by Kaplan-Meier with a joint longitudinal-survival model as sensitivity analysis. Mixed models for repeated measures on QLQ-C30 and EQ-5D-5L. Missing-not-at-random sensitivity analyses. The statistical analysis plan follows HTA formats, with frail versus non-frail comparison described but not adjusted for causal inference.","instrument":"EORTC QLQ-C30, QLQ-LC13, EQ-5D-5L, PRO-CTCAE, Zarit short form, G8, CFS; ePRO at baseline and months 1, 3, 6, 9 and 12.","study_design":"Frailty-enriched, PRO-intensive stratum embedded in the prospective multinational observational Velmara registry. Frailty screening at enrolment, ePRO with caregiver-assisted completion, and clinician-assessed frailty at each registry visit. The primary estimand is within-Velmara, with no external comparator. Frailty definitions and sites are shared with TAC-007.","gap_coverage":"Provides Velmara-specific frail-patient PRO and QoL evidence with validated instruments and an HTA-oriented analysis plan. It does not provide a comparative frail estimate versus other regimens.","cost_effort":"Low to moderate incremental cost on top of the registry: frailty screening, an ePRO licence and caregiver instruments, extra site training, and a dedicated analysis plan. No new site network, contracting or ethics submission beyond the registry.","timing":"Needs to be written into the registry protocol before first patient in. The interim cut is about 18 months after start and the primary cut about 24 months after start.","feasibility_risks":"The registry is planned, not yet running, so the module is a protocol addition before activation and needs a credible protocol amendment or revision, which has not been approved. Prospective enrolment is required. There is no post-hoc element. Risks include a small frail share at launch, ePRO attrition from death or deterioration (handled by the composite estimand), and community sites that do not screen for frailty. The module is within-Velmara only, so payers asking for a comparator would need the dedicated cohort.","post_hoc":false,"prospective_enrolment":true,"protocol_amendment":true,"start_date":null,"evidence_available":""},"comparative_rationale":"Versus a new dedicated frail PRO cohort (GAP-027:proposal:2): the expansion costs far less and starts earlier because it reuses registry sites, consent and data capture, but has no comparator and depends on registry activation and frail uptake. The dedicated cohort adds an exploratory comparator at much higher cost, with separate site set-up and later readout. Versus a new standalone within-Velmara PRO study: it would duplicate registry infrastructure for the same data. Versus extending TAC-013: that survey is not Velmara-specific and does not use HTA-grade instruments. Expansion is therefore the most efficient first step, with evidence quality of observational prospective single-arm data that payers will view as supportive and descriptive.","population":"Adults with EGFR-mutant advanced NSCLC starting Velmara as second-line therapy after osimertinib who are frail (G8 of 14 or lower confirmed by CFS 5 or above, or ECOG PS 2), at US and EU5 registry sites. calls.reply: {"tactics":[{"id":"GAP-020:proposal:1","gap_id":"GAP-020","name":"VEL-301 CNS sub-study: BICR RANO-BM intracranial response with extended MRI follow-up and numeric pre-specified adequacy thresholds for the velmaratinib arm","type":"subgroup_analysis","evidence_question":"Do blinded-independent-review intracranial response rate and duration of intracranial response in the velmaratinib arm of the VEL-301 CNS sub-study (about 70 patients with measurable brain metastases) meet pre-specified numeric adequacy thresholds for precision and maturity, with censoring at new anticancer therapy, and, if TAC-024 output is available, how much precision does pooling with VEL-201 add?","rationale":"Adding patients to a randomized trial's CNS sub-study is hard, so this expansion raises the information per patient and sets numeric thresholds that show whether the existing sub-study is adequate for a durability claim. It uses blinded central review, MRI that continues until intracranial progression, and a SAP addendum with explicit adequacy thresholds and a decision rule. It is a partial answer because it adds no patients. If the thresholds are not met, the result gates the new confirmatory cohort (GAP-020:proposal:2). The TAC-024 pooled comparison is optional and depends on TAC-024 output.","proposal_kind":"expansion","target_tactic_id":"TAC-010","expansion_scope":{"name":"VEL-301 CNS sub-study: BICR RANO-BM intracranial response with extended MRI follow-up and numeric pre-specified adequacy thresholds for the velmaratinib arm","evidence_question":"Do blinded-independent-review intracranial response rate and duration of intracranial response in the velmaratinib arm of the VEL-301 CNS sub-study (about 70 patients with measurable brain metastases) meet pre-specified numeric adequacy thresholds for precision and maturity, with censoring at new anticancer therapy, and, if TAC-024 output is available, how much precision does pooling with VEL-201 add?","population":"VEL-301 participants with at least one measurable brain metastasis (≥10 mm) per RANO-BM at baseline, including previously treated stable lesions. About 140 patients in total. Planning assumption under 1:1 randomization: about 70 per arm, to be confirmed against the CNS sub-study SAP. Adequacy thresholds apply to the velmaratinib arm (about 70). The comparator arm (about 70) is descriptive only.","outcomes":"Per-arm N and number of responders. BICR intracranial ORR with exact 95% CI. Median duration of intracranial response (Kaplan-Meier, 95% CI) and 6- and 12-month landmark durability, with censoring at start of new anticancer therapy. Intracranial PFS. Time to CNS progression. Observed CI bounds and half-widths against the numeric adequacy thresholds. Share of patients censored at new therapy. Share of baseline scans retrievable for retroactive BICR. BICR versus investigator-assessment concordance. Optional precision gain (CI half-width reduction) when the velmaratinib-arm data are combined with the TAC-024 pooled estimate.","geography":"US + EU5 VEL-301 sites","data_cut":"A CNS-specific data cut at least 6 months after the first response of the last responder, taken alongside or shortly after the primary PFS analysis. Pre-specified in the SAP addendum.","analysis":"SAP addendum with these elements. (1) Numeric adequacy thresholds for the velmaratinib arm, proposed for confirmation through payer/HTA scientific advice and not assumed agreed. (a) iORR: lower exact 95% CI bound ≥35% (about 50% observed with n≈70 gives a lower bound of about 38%). (b) Median DoR: lower 95% CI bound ≥6 months. (c) Maturity: ≥25 DoR events, and ≥80% of responders with ≥6 months of follow-up from first response. (d) Decision rule: gap treated as closed if a, b and c are met. Partially closed if only the iORR criterion is met. Not closed otherwise, which triggers the confirmatory cohort in GAP-020:proposal:2. Planning half-widths, to be confirmed by simulation: iORR about ±11-12 points, DoR about ±3.5-4 months. (2) Primary DoR censors at start of new anticancer therapy. Sensitivity analyses treat new therapy as an event and ignore it, and handle death and non-CNS progression as competing risks. The share of patients who have started new therapy is estimated from blinded trial data before the amendment is submitted. (3) A Bayesian posterior probability that median DoR exceeds a pre-set clinically meaningful threshold, as sensitivity only. (4) Optional precision-gain table, run only if TAC-024 output is available at the CNS data cut. It takes the pooled VEL-201 + VEL-301 estimate as an input and does not re-run it. VEL-201 used investigator assessment and VEL-301 uses BICR. The pooling is therefore treated as supportive, with the BICR versus investigator concordance measured in VEL-301 used to calibrate any discount, and VEL-301-only results stay primary. (5) Per-arm results shown descriptively, with no comparative efficacy claim.","instrument":"RANO-BM criteria applied through blinded independent central review of brain MRI","study_design":"Protocol amendment to the ongoing VEL-301 trial, with a SAP addendum, that (1) adds blinded independent central review of all CNS imaging by RANO-BM, including retroactive review of scans already acquired, after the imaging vendor confirms DICOM retention, (2) continues scheduled brain MRI after extracranial progression until intracranial progression or new anticancer therapy, (3) pre-specifies the numeric adequacy thresholds, the censoring rules, the decision rule and the CNS data cut, and (4) pre-specifies optional precision-gain reporting against the TAC-024 pooled estimate if available.","gap_coverage":"Partial but direct. It adds no patients. It increases the information per patient, removes investigator-assessment bias and, through the numeric thresholds and decision rule, states whether the existing sub-study is adequate for a durability claim. If the thresholds are not met, it triggers the new confirmatory cohort. It cannot by itself make a roughly 70-patient arm sufficient if the CIs stay wide.","cost_effort":"Low to moderate: imaging vendor scope change, amendment, SAP addendum and additional MRIs at existing sites. No new sites or enrolment.","timing":"Needs an amendment and ethics/regulatory notification, then runs alongside VEL-301 follow-up, with the readout at the CNS data cut. It cannot feed the 2027-03-31 US P&T decision, the 30 November 2026 CEA/BIM input freeze or the 15 January 2027 HTA elderly package. It can feed late-2027 EU5 HTA dossiers, later EU5 re-assessments and post-launch US payer updates. If retroactive reads on existing scans start early, a descriptive BICR iORR could be available earlier, but not a mature DoR.","feasibility_risks":"No amendment approval or imaging access is assumed. Retroactive BICR of scans already acquired is post-hoc (post_hoc is true) and depends on imaging retention, so retrievable scans are counted before commitment and any patient whose scans are unavailable falls back to investigator assessment as a sensitivity analysis. Only the extended MRI follow-up, BICR of newly acquired scans and the pre-specified data cut are prospective additions to existing participants. There is no new enrolment (prospective_enrolment is false) and a protocol amendment is required (protocol_amendment is true), but it is not yet approved. MRI after extracranial progression is confounded by later therapy, so DoR is censored at new therapy and the affected share is estimated first. The thresholds depend on payer/HTA feedback. Per-arm N of about 70 is a planning assumption, and the iORR may be lower than the VEL-201 52%.","post_hoc":true,"prospective_enrolment":false,"protocol_amendment":true,"start_date":null,"evidence_available":null},"comparative_rationale":"Evidence quality: the best available for the existing patients, because it is randomized-trial data with BICR and prospective follow-up. It cannot beat a larger sample for precision. Cost/effort: lower than a new cohort, with no new sites or enrolment. Time: the readout is tied to the CNS data cut and follows the 2027-03-31 decision, so it supports later dossiers and updates and not the first P&T and HTA filings. Feasibility: depends on amendment approval, imaging retention and MRI compliance. Alternatives: (a) a new single-arm cohort (GAP-020:proposal:2) adds patients but is slower and costlier, so it is gated on this tactic; (b) the pooled VEL-201 analysis is already TAC-024, so this tactic uses its output only as an optional input; (c) real-world CNS evidence is already TAC-011; (d) an indirect comparison does not fix sample precision. Recommended as the lowest-cost first step and as the gate for any new cohort.","population":"VEL-301 participants with at least one measurable brain metastasis (≥10 mm) per RANO-BM at baseline, including previously treated stable lesions. About 140 patients in total. Planning assumption under 1:1 randomization: about 70 per arm, to be confirmed against the CNS sub-study SAP. Adequacy thresholds apply to the velmaratinib arm (about 70). The comparator arm (about 70) is descriptive only.","comparator":"VEL-301 randomized comparator arm (osimertinib re-challenge or investigator's choice), shown descriptively; adequacy thresholds apply to the velmaratinib arm only","outcomes":"Per-arm N and number of responders. BICR intracranial ORR with exact 95% CI. Median duration of intracranial response (Kaplan-Meier, 95% CI) and 6- and 12-month landmark durability, with censoring at start of new anticancer therapy. Intracranial PFS. Time to CNS progression. Observed CI bounds and half-widths against the numeric adequacy thresholds. Share of patients censored at new therapy. Share of baseline scans retrievable for retroactive BICR. BICR versus investigator-assessment concordance. Optional precision gain (CI half-width reduction) when the velmaratinib-arm data are combined with the TAC-024 pooled estimate.","data_source":"VEL-301 trial data (prospective brain MRI plus retroactively centrally reviewed scans where retained); TAC-024 pooled VEL-201 + VEL-301 output as an optional input","study_design":"Protocol amendment to the ongoing VEL-301 trial, with a SAP addendum, that (1) adds blinded independent central review of all CNS imaging by RANO-BM, including retroactive review of scans already acquired, after the imaging vendor confirms DICOM retention, (2) continues scheduled brain MRI after extracranial progression until intracranial progression or new anticancer therapy, (3) pre-specifies the numeric adequacy thresholds, the censoring rules, the decision rule and the CNS data cut, and (4) pre-specifies optional precision-gain reporting against the TAC-024 pooled estimate if available.","duration_months":18,"readout_lag_months":4,"timing_rationale":"Duration covers the amendment and approvals, the imaging-retention check, retroactive central review, and the extra MRI follow-up until responders have matured to the CNS data cut. The lag covers BICR reads, CNS database lock, the SAP-specified analysis against the thresholds and QC of the dossier tables.","withdraw":false,"withdraw_reason":""},{"id":"GAP-020:proposal:2","gap_id":"GAP-020","name":"VEL-CNS: gated single-arm Phase IIIb confirmatory intracranial cohort in patients with measurable brain metastases after osimertinib","type":"phase3_trial","evidence_question":"If the VEL-301 CNS sub-study does not meet its pre-specified adequacy thresholds, what are BICR-assessed intracranial ORR and duration of intracranial response with velmaratinib in an independent prospective cohort of about 80 patients with measurable brain metastases after osimertinib, and does discounted pooling with the VEL-301 velmaratinib arm reach the target precision?","rationale":"A separate prospective cohort adds about 80 patients with measurable brain metastases and gives independent BICR replication of the intracranial response and duration. Stand-alone, 80 patients give about the same CI width as the VEL-301 sub-study, so the main value is replication plus the narrower pooled interval. The cohort is gated on the TAC-010 expansion (GAP-020:proposal:1), so it is only started if the existing sub-study is judged inadequate. Because both datasets use BICR RANO-BM, pooling is more credible than pooling with investigator-assessed VEL-201.","proposal_kind":"new","target_tactic_id":null,"expansion_scope":null,"comparative_rationale":"Evidence quality: prospective, protocol-driven imaging with BICR, stronger than real-world data (TAC-011) but with no concurrent control, so it supports a durability claim and not comparative superiority. Cost/effort: the highest of the options, a new multinational study with about 470 patients screened at about 40 sites, which is why it is gated. Time: slowest, with a readout about 38 months after start, so it cannot feed the 2027-03-31 decision. Its iORR interim and final readout can support later EU5 HTA re-assessments and US payer updates in 2028-2029. Feasibility: moderate, with competition from osimertinib and NX-441 trials and from commercial use after approval. Alternatives: a CNS cohort nested in the registry (TAC-021) is cheaper but would overlap TAC-011 and TAC-024 and have heterogeneous imaging, so it is not proposed as a separate tactic. Expanding TAC-010 (proposal 1) is cheaper and faster but adds no patients, so it is the gate. Not a duplicate of TAC-010, TAC-011 or TAC-024, because it adds a new prospective BICR-assessed cohort. The phase3_trial type is the nearest available type for a single-arm Phase IIIb interventional cohort.","population":"Adults with EGFR-mutant advanced NSCLC progressing after osimertinib, with at least one measurable brain metastasis (≥10 mm) per RANO-BM, ECOG 0-2, about 80 patients, with a target of at least 30% aged 65 or over. Key secondary: duration of intracranial response (median, 6- and 12-month landmark), intracranial PFS, time to CNS progression, CNS-directed radiotherapy use, neurocognitive and symptom PRO (EORTC QLQ-BN20), and ILD and QT safety. Target precision, set in advance as the gate criterion: pooled iORR 95% CI half-width ≤±9 points (VEL-301 velmaratinib arm plus cohort, discounted) and a pooled median DoR lower 95% bound that can be compared with the ≥6-month threshold. Stand-alone expected: iORR half-width about ±11 points and DoR half-width about ±3.5-4 months with about 40 responders.","data_source":"New prospective single-arm study at about 40 US and EU5 neuro-oncology and thoracic centres, with central MRI review, using VEL-301 CNS BICR results as the benchmark and pooling input","study_design":"Open-label, single-arm, multicentre Phase IIIb interventional cohort, started only if the TAC-010 expansion (GAP-020:proposal:1) shows that the velmaratinib-arm adequacy thresholds are not met (lower iORR 95% bound <35%, or median DoR lower bound <6 months, or <25 DoR events). Site feasibility and start-up can run at risk in parallel while that gate readout is pending, with no enrolment before the decision. Velmaratinib is not yet approved at plan date, so it starts as a pre-approval study and moves to post-marketing in each country as approval is granted. BICR RANO-BM, MRI every 8 weeks until intracranial progression or new anticancer therapy, and an iORR-only interim at 12 months (no median DoR claim). The primary analysis is stand-alone. A secondary Bayesian pooled estimate with the VEL-301 velmaratinib arm uses a robust meta-analytic-predictive prior with a pre-specified discount (power-prior weight ≤0.5, sensitivity at 0, 0.25, 0.5 and 1). VEL-201 enters only as a further sensitivity input because of investigator assessment. Enrolment mitigation: a 9-month enrolment review with rolling addition of sites, referral from multidisciplinary neuro-oncology clinics and registry (TAC-021) sites, and access to the study ahead of and alongside commercial availability. A futility and feasibility review can stop the study if enrolment is below about 50% of plan.","duration_months":34,"readout_lag_months":4,"timing_rationale":"About 6 months for protocol, ethics and site activation across the US and EU5. About 10 months of follow-up after the last patient in. With a VEL-201 median DoR of 9.7 months and about 40 responders enrolled throughout, this is expected to yield about 25 DoR events and ≥6 months of follow-up in most responders. calls.reply: {"tactics":[{"id":"GAP-021:proposal:2","gap_id":"GAP-021","name":"US specialty pharmacy dispensing interim persistence bridge for Velmara (not the claims-based answer)","type":"rwe_study","evidence_question":"What are early fill-based persistence and time-to-first-missed-refill signals for Velmara in the first months after US launch, using specialty pharmacy dispensing data, and how do they align at aggregate level with the later claims-based persistence estimate in TAC-008?","rationale":"Claims data lag several months after launch, while specialty pharmacy and hub dispensing data arrive within weeks of a fill. This descriptive bridge gives a directional signal about 5 months after launch, ahead of TAC-008. It is labelled an interim bridge and must not be presented to P&T as the claims-based persistence answer, which stays with TAC-008. This revision responds to the four objections: it uses a shorter gap for the 3-month cut, relabels the study as a bridge, adds a partner shortlist with a coverage go/no-go and a fallback, and makes aggregate-level alignment the default.","proposal_kind":"new","target_tactic_id":null,"expansion_scope":null,"comparative_rationale":"A new tactic versus expanding TAC-008. Expanding TAC-008 would inherit its claims run-out lag, which defeats the purpose of an early signal. The dispensing feed also differs from claims in source, coverage and timing, so it is kept separate and framed as a bridge, not a second answer to the same question. Evidence quality is lower than claims: it is descriptive, covers only participating channels, has no comparator and lacks clinical covariates, and leakage can bias persistence downward. A coverage estimate and leakage sensitivity analyses mitigate this. Incremental cost is low to moderate, mainly a data feed and an analysis. Time is its advantage, since the first cut is available about 5 months after launch versus roughly 9 months or more for claims. Feasibility depends on securing a partner, which is not yet confirmed. A go/no-go gate and a fallback are included, and it does not replace TAC-008.","population":"Adults with a Velmara dispense in the US specialty pharmacy or hub dispensing feed from the first launch fill onward. A Velmara dispense is taken to imply the indicated population, because diagnosis is often not recorded in dispensing feeds. Diagnosis is used as a sensitivity restriction where recorded, and the age 65+ cut is reported only where age is available.","comparator":"None — descriptive; published osimertinib persistence is used only as an informal external reference and is not a formal comparison","outcomes":"3-month interim cut: proportion with continued fills at 3 months using a 30-day permissible gap, and time to first missed refill (Kaplan-Meier), with refill intervals. 6-month cut: proportion persistent at 6 months using a 60-day permissible gap, matching TAC-008, with a 45-day sensitivity analysis, plus discontinuation and median time to discontinuation. Coverage and leakage: estimated share of Velmara dispensing captured by the feed, and persistence under leakage-adjusted scenarios. Alignment: aggregate-level comparison of 6-month persistence with the TAC-008 estimate once available.","data_source":"A US specialty pharmacy or hub dispensing feed under a data-sharing agreement. No partner is identified or confirmed. The shortlist of partner types to approach before launch is (a) a commercial specialty pharmacy dispensing aggregator, (b) a national specialty pharmacy network or the largest specialty pharmacies directly, and (c) the manufacturer's own hub or patient-services vendor. Go/no-go: proceed only if the feed is estimated to capture at least 60% of Velmara dispensing, assessed by reconciling feed units against shipped or sold units within 8 weeks of launch. Fallback if coverage is below 60% or no agreement is reached by launch: report only the hub-enrolled cohort, labelled as selected and non-representative, or stop the bridge and rely on TAC-008. Aggregate-level alignment with TAC-008 is the default. Patient-level tokenised linkage is not assumed and would be added only if both data owners agree.","study_design":"Descriptive retrospective cohort of Velmara initiators identified from dispensing data, with the index date at first fill. Readout schedule from launch: the 3-month cut is a data cut at launch plus 3 months, reported about 5 months post-launch. The 6-month cut is a data cut at launch plus 6 months, reported about 8 months post-launch. A final cut follows at 12 months. The 3-month cut uses the 30-day gap and time to first missed refill, because a 60-day gap is uninformative at 90 days. The 6-month cut uses the 60-day gap. A coverage analysis estimates feed capture from unit reconciliation, and leakage sensitivity analyses assume a range of channel-switch rates among apparent discontinuers. Results are reported by payer type and, where age is recorded, age 65+. Every output is labelled 'interim dispensing-based bridge, not claims-based persistence' and is routed to P&T only as a bridge alongside the TAC-008 timeline.","duration_months":12,"readout_lag_months":2,"timing_rationale":"Launch is 2027-H1, and 12 months of accrual from launch gives all early initiators at least 6 months of follow-up and a representative cohort, with a final cut at 12 months. Dispensing feeds arrive within weeks, so cleaning, coverage estimation and analysis take about 2 months per cut. This puts the 3-month readout at about 5 months post-launch and the 6-month readout at about 8 months post-launch. Neither can inform the 2027-03-31 decision, which precedes launch, so they serve post-launch P&T reviews and formulary updates."},{"id":"GAP-021:proposal:1","gap_id":"GAP-021","name":"TAC-008 expansion: active-comparator persistence benchmark with payer-segment stratification","type":"rwe_study","evidence_question":"How does six-month persistence on Velmara in US claims compare with persistence on osimertinib and NX-441 in post-osimertinib EGFR-mutant NSCLC, stratified by payer type and age 65+?","rationale":"US payers distrust trial persistence, and a Velmara-only rate has no reference point. P&T committees can interpret persistence only against what patients do on alternatives, so a claims-based estimate benchmarked against active comparators and split by payer segment is more decision-useful than an isolated figure.","proposal_kind":"expansion","target_tactic_id":"TAC-008","expansion_scope":{"name":"TAC-008 expansion: active-comparator persistence benchmark with payer-segment stratification","evidence_question":"How does six-month persistence on Velmara in US claims compare with persistence on osimertinib and NX-441 in post-osimertinib EGFR-mutant NSCLC, stratified by payer type and age 65+?","population":"Adults with NSCLC and a prior osimertinib claim who initiate Velmara, osimertinib re-treatment or NX-441 as new users, with at least 6 months of continuous enrolment before the index date. Comparator arms are reported only if at least 100 initiators per arm are reached, otherwise descriptive only.","instrument":"Pharmacy and medical claims algorithm for the EGFR-mutant NSCLC post-osimertinib population, using diagnosis codes, prior osimertinib claims and oral antineoplastic NDCs, with the algorithm validated against a chart-confirmed subset where available.","study_design":"Retrospective new-user, active-comparator cohort study in US closed adjudicated claims, with IPTW adjustment and prespecified payer-type and age strata.","gap_coverage":"Extends the base Velmara-only persistence estimate to a benchmarked, payer-stratified answer, which is more directly usable by P&T committees. It needs comparator extraction, weighting, strata and a validation sub-sample, but no new data source and no enrolment.","timing":"Adds about 2 months of analysis to the base claims readout. The comparative cut is not available until at least 6 months of follow-up after launch plus claims lag.","feasibility_risks":"NX-441 uptake may be too low for a stable comparison, so comparators are reported only above a prespecified size. TAC-008 is accepted but only proposed, so these design additions can be made before it starts without a protocol amendment. No data access or contract is assumed to be approved. This is not post hoc, there is no prospective enrolment and no protocol amendment is required.","post_hoc":false,"prospective_enrolment":false,"protocol_amendment":false,"start_date":null,"evidence_available":""},"comparative_rationale":"Expansion of TAC-008 versus a new standalone comparative claims study. A new study would duplicate the same claims extraction, cohort build and data licence, adding cost and a second parallel readout. Expansion reuses TAC-008's infrastructure, with only incremental analysis cost. Evidence quality is higher than a descriptive rate because an active-comparator, IPTW-adjusted design gives context and partly controls confounding, though residual confounding and small comparator numbers remain. Time is slower than the specialty pharmacy bridge (GAP-021:proposal:2): about 9 to 12 months after launch for the first comparative readout, versus about 5 months for the bridge. Feasibility is good for Velmara versus osimertinib and uncertain for NX-441. The two tactics are complementary: the bridge gives the early signal and this expansion gives the benchmarked claims answer.","population":"Adults with NSCLC and a prior osimertinib claim who initiate Velmara, osimertinib re-treatment or NX-441 as new users, with at least 6 months of continuous enrolment before the index date. Strata: commercial, Medicare Part D and Medicaid, and age 65+ versus under 65.","comparator":"Osimertinib re-treatment new users and NX-441 new users after prior osimertinib","outcomes":"Primary: six-month persistence with a 60-day permissible gap. Secondary: 30-day-gap sensitivity, time to discontinuation, proportion of days covered, switching and re-initiation, and adjusted hazard ratio of discontinuation versus each comparator. Results are reported by payer type and age 65+.","data_source":"US closed adjudicated pharmacy and medical claims database, the same source planned for TAC-008. Licence and access are not yet confirmed.","study_design":"Retrospective new-user, active-comparator cohort study in US closed adjudicated claims, with IPTW adjustment and prespecified payer-type and age strata.","duration_months":15,"readout_lag_months":3,"timing_rationale":"Launch is 2027-H1. Follow-up of at least 6 months for early initiators plus accrual through 12 months after launch gives enough comparator volume, and a closed-claims run-out lag of about 3 months applies to the last cut. The extra analysis of weighting and strata adds about a month to the standard claims readout. The first comparative readout therefore falls well after the 2027-03-31 decision date, so it supports post-launch P&T reviews."}]}

calls.reply: {"tactics":[{"id":"GAP-023:proposal:1","gap_id":"GAP-023","name":"Target trial emulation of velmaratinib versus regional platinum-based or single-agent chemotherapy in patients aged 65+ using VEL-201 and VEL-301 IPD and a US/EU5 real-world comparator","type":"rwe_study","evidence_question":"After adjustment for baseline confounding and eligibility alignment, how does overall survival with velmaratinib compare with regional active systemic standard of care (platinum-based doublet chemotherapy or single-agent chemotherapy) in patients aged 65 and over with EGFR-mutant NSCLC progressing on osimertinib, with best supportive care assessed separately?","rationale":"Payers and HTA bodies regard the VEL-301 elderly subgroup as descriptive and say no adjusted comparison against regional SoC exists. TAC-007 holds this question as a placeholder with no design. This tactic gives it a prespecified, staged target trial emulation with explicit comparator justification, eligibility alignment, time-zero and immortal-time handling, a go/no-go on sample size and quantified bias analyses. This revision responds to the objection on overall survival. EHR-derived data under-capture deaths, which biases the real-world arm towards longer survival. The revision adds linkage to mortality sources and a minimum death-capture requirement, and specifies how VEL-201 and VEL-301 patients are pooled, with a heterogeneity check by study. It is not a powered randomised comparison. The full result will arrive after the 15 Jan 2027 HTA package and the 31 Mar 2027 decision.","proposal_kind":"expansion","target_tactic_id":"TAC-007","expansion_scope":{"name":"Target trial emulation of velmaratinib versus regional platinum-based or single-agent chemotherapy in patients aged 65+ using VEL-201 and VEL-301 IPD and a US/EU5 real-world comparator","evidence_question":"After adjustment for baseline confounding and eligibility alignment, how does overall survival with velmaratinib compare with regional active systemic standard of care (platinum-based doublet chemotherapy or single-agent chemotherapy) in patients aged 65 and over with EGFR-mutant NSCLC progressing on osimertinib, with best supportive care assessed separately?","population":"Adults aged 65 years and over with EGFR-mutant advanced NSCLC and documented progression on prior osimertinib, ECOG 0-1, and brain metastases handled per VEL-301/VEL-201 eligibility (treated or stable and asymptomatic), so that real-world patients are aligned to trial eligibility. Velmaratinib arm: VEL-201 participants and VEL-301 velmaratinib-arm participants aged 65+. Comparator arm: patients aged 65+ meeting the same criteria who started regional systemic SoC as the first treatment after osimertinib in routine care in the US and EU5. Best supportive care-only patients form a separate sensitivity cohort and are not pooled with the comparator arm.","outcomes":"Primary: overall survival from time zero (first dose of velmaratinib or of SoC as the first treatment after osimertinib), reported as an adjusted hazard ratio with 95% CI. Secondary: time to treatment discontinuation or death, and adjusted restricted mean survival time difference at a prespecified horizon. Descriptive only, within the real-world cohort: real-world PFS, which is not compared with trial-assessed PFS. Bias and data-quality outputs: E-values and quantitative bias analysis for unmeasured confounding, death-capture sensitivity by real-world data source, and a heterogeneity assessment between VEL-201 and VEL-301 velmaratinib patients.","geography":"US and EU5 (France, Germany, Italy, Spain, UK), reported by region for HTA","data_cut":"Stage 1: final clean VEL-201 data (completed study) and the latest refresh of licensed oncology EHR-derived datasets with mortality linkage. Stage 2: VEL-301 velmaratinib-arm data from the event-driven Q4 2027 interim OS cut (or a later cut if OS is still immature), released to an independent statistician under a firewall. Exact cut dates to be set in the protocol.","analysis":"Protocol and SAP are written before any outcome analysis, from a target trial specification (eligibility, treatment strategies, time zero, follow-up, causal contrast). Time zero is treatment start of the first post-osimertinib line in both arms, with a documented osimertinib progression date required. To limit immortal-time bias, real-world patients must have been alive and untreated for the same progression-to-treatment interval seen in trial patients, and a landmark sensitivity analysis is run. Overlap or inverse-probability-of-treatment weighting is applied on prespecified confounders (ECOG, comorbidity, brain metastases, number of metastatic sites, prior lines, time on and response to osimertinib, EGFR variant, region, index year). Covariate balance, region-stratified analyses, negative-control outcomes, E-values and quantitative bias analysis are reported. OS is the only outcome compared between trial and real-world data. MORTALITY CAPTURE: the real-world arm may use only sources with validated mortality. In the US, EHR-derived records are linked to a composite mortality source (commercial death data combined with Social Security and obituary data, with National Death Index linkage where feasible). In EU5, records are linked to national or regional death registries where legally and technically possible (for example national health-data or statistics-office death records). A minimum death-capture sensitivity is required for inclusion in the primary analysis, proposed at 90% or higher against a reference mortality source and to be confirmed by biostatistics. Sources below the threshold are excluded from the primary analysis and used only in a sensitivity analysis. Death-capture sensitivity is reported by source and region. Sensitivity analyses include censoring at last-activity date and probabilistic correction for under-captured deaths. POOLING: the SAP specifies that VEL-201 (single-arm Phase II) and VEL-301 velmaratinib-arm patients are pooled with study as a stratification variable and covariate. Heterogeneity is checked with study-level Kaplan-Meier curves, study-specific adjusted hazard ratios with a forest plot, a study-by-treatment interaction test and baseline comparability tables. If material heterogeneity is found, the primary analysis is restricted to VEL-301 velmaratinib patients (or uses a random-effects approach), and the pooled result becomes a sensitivity analysis. Pre-specified go/no-go: proceed to the adjusted hazard-ratio analysis only if there are at least 50 velmaratinib-treated patients aged 65+ (VEL-201 plus VEL-301) and a weighted effective sample size of at least 100 in the comparator arm, with at least 60 expected OS events after applying the mortality-capture restriction. These thresholds are proposed and need biostatistics confirmation. They give a precision-based estimate (95% CI roughly x/÷1.7 around the HR at 60 events), not a powered confirmatory test. If the thresholds are not met, only a descriptive and balance report is issued. Comparator justification: platinum-based doublet chemotherapy is the primary comparator as the usual post-osimertinib option in fit patients in both regions. Single-agent chemotherapy forms a separate stratum for patients judged platinum-ineligible, where practice varies by country. Regional add-on agents are tabulated. calls.reply: {"reviews":[{"id":"GAP-034:proposal:1","verdict":"keep","confidence":80,"note":"Sound expansion of TAC-015, and the only option that gives randomised OS versus the VEL-301 control arm (ITT, pre-specified maturity cuts, RPSFT/IPCW sensitivity analyses). The added scope is legitimate: TAC-015 has no milestones, switching adjustment or decision rules, and TAC-027 only covers publication. Before finalising: (1) set a real start_date. It is null, and the 54-month window and the 2029-2031 cuts depend on it. (2) Confirm against the VEL-301 protocol whether subsequent-therapy and crossover data are captured, since the adjusted analyses fail without them. (3) Keep the plan explicit that only the follow-up plan, not OS data, is available for the 2027 decisions, because the Q4 2027 interim falls after 2027-03-31. The 4-month readout lag and the 60-month descriptive-only landmark are credible. Do not treat the amendment as approved.","issues":[],"duplicate_of":null},{"id":"GAP-034:proposal:2","verdict":"revise","confidence":50,"note":"This is not a duplicate of TAC-020. OS tails and extrapolation benchmarking is valid added scope, but the tactic does not close the gap: no velmaratinib OS and no follow-up plan. Position it explicitly as a supporting tactic for CEA/HTA modelling (TAC-004), not as a gap-closing tactic. Changes: (1) Timing. About 11 months misses the 30 Nov 2026 CEA input freeze and the Jan-Mar 2027 HTA/P&T dates, so state which decision it actually serves or cut scope to meet the freeze. (2) Feasibility. 8 months to license and harmonise five national sources is optimistic, and access is unconfirmed for all of them. Restrict the primary design to Flatiron plus one or two EU sources with a confirmed access path, and move CRISP, ESME and NCRAS to optional until access is confirmed. Or extend duration_months to about 12. (3) Dependency. TAC-020 is planned with no start date, so make the stand-alone cohort build the base case and treat sharing the TAC-020 cohort as an upside. (4) Comparison. Benchmarking against an immature Q4 2027 control arm that has few events is weak. Pre-specify what fit result would change the extrapolation choice, or drop that comparison and limit the study to the observed RWE tail. Keep the exclusion of osimertinib re-challenge patients and the at-risk threshold for the 36-month landmark.","issues":["gap_coverage","timing","data_access","dependency","weak_validation"],"duplicate_of":null}]}

calls.reply: {"reviews":[{"id":"GAP-027:proposal:1","verdict":"keep","confidence":72,"note":"Holds as an expansion of TAC-021. The registry is planned and not yet running, so a pre-start protocol revision is credible, though it has not been approved. The added scope is valid: a frailty-defined quota, HTA-accepted instruments (QLQ-C30, EQ-5D-5L, Zarit) and an in-registry fit comparator. It is Velmara-specific and longitudinal, which TAC-013 is not. The 24-month duration and 4-month lag are consistent with recruiting about 150 frail patients plus 12 months of follow-up. Before finalising: (1) add a sample-size or precision rationale for 150 frail versus 150 fit, since the primary outcome is change to month 6 and death and attrition will be high; (2) state the registry start date as a dependency in `timing`; (3) fix the frailty definition and align it with any other frail-population tactic.","issues":[],"duplicate_of":null},{"id":"GAP-027:proposal:2","verdict":"revise","confidence":45,"note":"This is a reasonable conditional fallback but overlaps the registry frail module (proposal 1) on the same Velmara frail PRO question. Revise as follows. (1) Define the trigger in the design, for example 'registry frail module below X patients at month Y, or an HTA body requests a comparative frail PRO estimate'. The current gate only tests this study's own enrolment. (2) Add a rule against double enrolment with the registry, or a link to it. The protocol currently covers only TAC-007, so the same frail Velmara starters could be counted in both studies. (3) Align the frailty definition with the registry: 'G8 ≤14 confirmed by CFS ≥5, or ECOG PS 2' conflicts with 'ECOG PS ≥2'. (4) Re-check the recruitment assumption: about 100 frail Velmara starters in 15 months at launch is optimistic, so the 40-patient gate at month 12 should drive the plan. (5) Keep the comparison explicitly exploratory. A within-Velmara composite estimand is acceptable, but a deterioration-or-death endpoint without a comparator needs an interpretation plan.","issues":["overlap_with_registry_module","trigger_undefined","frailty_definition_inconsistent","recruitment_feasibility"],"duplicate_of":null},{"id":"GAP-029:proposal:1","verdict":"keep","confidence":72,"note":"Valid expansion of TAC-009, not a duplicate. The parent has no defined NX-441 or platinum-chemotherapy cohorts, no 65+ or brain-metastasis strata, no TTD, TTNT or OS endpoints and no adjusted analysis. This child adds all of them. A retrospective EHR or claims cohort is the right design for real-world pathways, and post_hoc=true with no enrolment or amendment is consistent. The gate (≥50 per arm with ≥6 months of follow-up, strata below 30 descriptive only, cells under 11 suppressed) handles the main risk that velmaratinib starters are near zero after launch. NX-441 and chemotherapy pathways are reported regardless. The 9-month timeline depends on licences and governance across US and EU5 being in place within about 3 months, which is optimistic and not confirmed. The phased US-first cut mitigates this. Tighten two points: state how OS is captured (linked mortality versus EHR-recorded death) and which databases are being considered.","issues":["data_access_unconfirmed","os_capture_unspecified"],"duplicate_of":null},{"id":"GAP-029:proposal:2","verdict":"drop","confidence":20,"note":"The tactic's own rationale says it does not close GAP-029, which asks for real-world pathways and outcomes after NX-441 or chemotherapy. A trial-based unanchored MAIC cannot supply pathways or real-world outcomes. The design also has weaknesses. VEL-201 is a single-arm Phase II (n=112) compared with published aggregate arms by ORR and DoR across heterogeneous post-osimertinib populations. DoR needs reconstructed data. The 29-patient CNS subset will probably fail the ESS gate. There may be no published NX-441 post-osimertinib trial arm to match, so the gate may stop it. Output labelled 'not HTA-grade' adds little. If an indirect-comparison need is later raised as its own gap, re-home this tactic there (ideally using VEL-301 data) instead of tying it to GAP-029.","issues":["gap_mismatch","comparator","unanchored_high_bias","population_heterogeneity","feasibility"],"duplicate_of":null}]}

calls.reply: {"reviews":[{"id":"GAP-001:proposal:1","verdict":"keep","confidence":70,"note":"A retrospective US claims cohort is the right design for observed procedure-level payer cost and HCRU of recurrence. It is a valid expansion of TAC-006, which has no population, source or design, so it is not a duplicate. The recurrence and EGFR proxies are handled with sensitivity analyses S1-S3 and a stratum rule. Data volume and the 3+1 month timing are credible once data access is in place. One fix to timing: study_design starts 2026-07-06 but allows data access to be executed as late as 2026-08-14. A 3-month build from mid-August misses the 2026-10-30 interim table. Move the access checkpoint to about 2026-07-31, or state that the interim table uses a preliminary extract built from the first 60% of the cohort. Keep the EU5 limitation explicit, with the micro-costing tactic covering EU5.","issues":["timing_checkpoint_inconsistency"],"duplicate_of":null},{"id":"GAP-001:proposal:2","verdict":"keep","confidence":62,"note":"This is a reasonable fallback and benchmark, and the proposal is honest about it. A pre-registered targeted SLR plus CMS fee-schedule micro-costing, with graded evidence and Delphi input, gives a transparent CEA-ready input by the 30 November 2026 freeze. It is also the only route to EU5 tariff inputs. It is modelled rather than routine-practice evidence, so it should not replace the claims study as the primary answer. Per-input evidence grades and the planned >25% difference check against the claims results address that limitation. It is not a duplicate of TAC-006 or of proposal 1, since the data and methods differ. Expect most procedure-frequency inputs to grade C or D because published post-osimertinib data are sparse. Note that in the CEA's probabilistic sensitivity analysis.","issues":[],"duplicate_of":null},{"id":"GAP-020:proposal:1","verdict":"revise","confidence":58,"note":"The design is sound as a low-cost first step: BICR RANO-BM, extended MRI follow-up, numeric adequacy thresholds, a decision rule and a gate for further evidence. It is a valid expansion of TAC-010 and adds scope without adding patients. The defect is in `data_cut` and `analysis`: the cut is fixed at ≥6 months after the last responder's first response, but the maturity criterion requires ≥25 DoR events. With about 35 responders and a VEL-201 median DoR of 9.7 months, a 6-month fixed cut will give far fewer than 25 events, so criterion (c) cannot be met and the gap would always read as 'not closed'. Make the data cut event-driven (≥25 DoR events or a fixed late date, whichever is first). Alternatively, relax the maturity criterion to a follow-up and landmark-based one, and restate the expected event count. Also state how the thresholds are fixed before unblinded CNS data are seen, because the trial is ongoing and retroactive BICR is post-hoc. Keep the TAC-024 pooling as an optional, supportive input only.","issues":["data_cut","maturity_criterion_unachievable","post_hoc_threshold_governance"],"duplicate_of":null},{"id":"GAP-020:proposal:2","verdict":"revise","confidence":42,"note":"The cohort is a credible replication design: single-arm, BICR, about 80 patients, with discounted pooling against the VEL-301 arm. It is not a duplicate of TAC-010, TAC-011 or TAC-024. The main problem is the gate. It depends on the proposal-1 readout, which comes about 22 months after its start (18 + 4). A 34 + 4 month study then reads out about 5 years from now, too late for any payer or HTA filing it is meant to support. Standalone it gives about the same CI width as the existing sub-study, so the extra value is small relative to the cost of 40 sites. Revise the `study_design`: either gate on an earlier decision point, such as a retroactive BICR iORR and DoR-maturity check on the existing scans, or run site start-up and enrolment in parallel with a futility stop. Rebase `timing_rationale` on the actual decision date. The type 'phase3_trial' is also a poor fit for a single-arm Phase IIIb cohort, so record this as a custom type if allowed.","issues":["gate_timing","time_to_readout","low_incremental_precision","type_mismatch"],"duplicate_of":null}]}

calls.reply: {"reviews":[{"id":"GAP-021:proposal:1","verdict":"keep","confidence":72,"note":"Sound expansion of TAC-008. A new-user, active-comparator claims cohort answers the payer ask for routine-care persistence and adds a yardstick. The persistence gap rule is limited to oral products, and chemotherapy is reported descriptively from administration records. Algorithm validation (PPV of at least 80%), a minimum of 100 initiators for adjusted NX-441 comparison and the 65+ stratum make the added scope credible. The timing arithmetic holds: 9 months of accrual plus 6 months of follow-up gives 15 months, plus 4 months of lag. It is honest that nothing on Velmara persistence can inform the 2027-03-31 decision. Before finalising, confirm Medicare Advantage capture and database licensing. Consider stating up front that early 65+ estimates will probably be descriptive only.","issues":[],"duplicate_of":null},{"id":"GAP-021:proposal:2","verdict":"revise","confidence":55,"note":"Not a duplicate of TAC-008. The source (dispensing feed), purpose (early bridge) and timing differ, and it is explicitly not presented as the claims-based answer. The readout schedule in study_design and timing_rationale is flawed, though. A '3-month cut at launch+3' and a '6-month cut at launch+6' leave almost nobody with full 3 or 6 months of follow-up, because only first-day fillers qualify. Fix by defining an initiator entry window for each cut (for example, patients initiating in launch months 1-2, with the 6-month cut at about launch+8 and readout about launch+10). Alternatively, report Kaplan-Meier persistence with censoring and state the minimum at-risk numbers. Then restate the 'about 5 and 8 months post-launch' claims. The partner shortlist, the 60% coverage go/no-go and the fallback are good and should stay. Also note that the 'dispense implies indicated population' assumption cannot be validated without diagnosis data.","issues":["duration","readout_timing","population"],"duplicate_of":null},{"id":"GAP-023:proposal:1","verdict":"keep","confidence":66,"note":"A credible, staged target-trial emulation. It uses an aligned eligibility set, clear time zero and immortal-time handling, platinum doublet as primary comparator with single-agent chemotherapy and BSC separated, and a go/no-go (at least 50 velmaratinib patients aged 65+, effective sample size of at least 100, at least 60 events). Mortality linkage with a 90% death-capture threshold addresses the main OS bias in EHR data. Pooling VEL-201 and VEL-301 with a heterogeneity check is specified. The post_hoc and amendment flags are correct, and it does not claim the 15 Jan 2027 or 31 Mar 2027 dates can be met. Tighten two points. Add a calendar-period (index-year) control or restriction for the VEL-201 versus contemporaneous RWD comparison. Justify excluding NX-441 patients from the comparator if NX-441 is regional standard of care, since this limits relevance to HTA. The design is not powered, so describe it as precision-based supportive evidence.","issues":[],"duplicate_of":null},{"id":"GAP-023:proposal:2","verdict":"revise","confidence":50,"note":"A reasonable lower-cost EU5 complement, and not a duplicate of TAC-003 or TAC-025. The linked comparator-cohort protocol leaves the running review and its publication timeline untouched. Two changes are needed. First, OS is the primary outcome but death ascertainment is not addressed. Hospital chart abstraction misses deaths outside the centre, which biases OS in the same way proposal 1 had to fix. Add vital-status verification via national or regional death registries or population registers, with a minimum capture requirement. Second, the go/no-go (at least 30 velmaratinib patients aged 65+, comparator at least twice that) supports only a very imprecise HR. With a median follow-up under 9 months, also expected, the primary result will really be a 6-month landmark or RMST. Make the 6-month landmark survival and RMST the primary estimand, report hazard ratios as exploratory, and state the expected precision. Keep the no-US-component limitation explicit, since the gap covers US payers too.","issues":["outcomes","data_source","power"],"duplicate_of":null}]}

Trigger (defined in the protocol): the registry frail module has enrolled fewer than 40 frail Velmara starters with baseline PRO at module month 12, or an HTA body or national payer has requested a comparative frail PRO estimate in writing. Anti-duplication: patients carry a single unique identifier checked against the registry screening log. A patient enrolled in the registry frail module cannot be enrolled here. Registry sites may refer eligible frail patients, who give consent for linked registry core data, and pooled frail analyses are de-duplicated by that identifier. Methods are Kaplan-Meier cumulative incidence of deterioration and death separately, restricted mean time to deterioration-or-death, mixed models for repeated measures, a joint longitudinal-survival model and missing-not-at-random sensitivity analyses. Interpretation plan: without a comparator, the composite endpoint is not read as efficacy. It is interpreted alongside its components, published frail-population benchmarks and the exploratory comparator. Enrolment gate: at study month 12 (9 months of recruitment), at least 40 Velmara frail patients must be enrolled, otherwise the study stops and reports the registry module only. calls.reply: {"tactics":[{"id":"GAP-021:proposal:2","gap_id":"GAP-021","name":"US specialty pharmacy dispensing interim persistence bridge for Velmara (not the claims-based answer)","type":"rwe_study","evidence_question":"What are early fill-based persistence and time-to-first-missed-refill signals for Velmara among US initiators in defined launch-month entry windows, using specialty pharmacy dispensing data, and how do they align at aggregate level with the later claims-based persistence estimate in TAC-008?","rationale":"Claims data lag several months after launch, while specialty pharmacy and hub dispensing data arrive within weeks. A descriptive bridge can give a directional signal before the claims-based TAC-008 estimate. This revision fixes the follow-up flaw: each cut now uses an initiator entry window, so every patient counted has the full 3 or 6 months of potential follow-up. Kaplan-Meier methods with censoring are used, and minimum at-risk numbers are reported. Timing claims are restated accordingly (about 7 and 11 months post-launch). The bridge stays labelled as interim and is never presented to P&T as the claims-based persistence answer, which remains with TAC-008. The partner shortlist, the 60% coverage go/no-go and the fallback are retained.","proposal_kind":"new","target_tactic_id":null,"expansion_scope":null,"comparative_rationale":"A new tactic versus expanding TAC-008. Expanding TAC-008 would inherit its claims run-out lag, which defeats the purpose of an early signal. The dispensing feed differs from claims in source, coverage and timing, so it is kept separate and framed as a bridge. Evidence quality is lower than claims. It is descriptive, covers only participating channels, has no comparator, has no clinical covariates and cannot verify diagnosis. Leakage can bias persistence downward. Coverage estimation, leakage sensitivity analyses and minimum at-risk reporting mitigate this. Incremental cost is low to moderate, mainly a data feed plus analysis. Time is its advantage: the 3-month readout is about launch+7 months and the 6-month readout about launch+11 months, versus roughly 12 months or more for a mature claims cut. Feasibility hinges on securing a partner, which is not confirmed. A go/no-go gate and a fallback are built in. It does not replace TAC-008.","population":"Adults with a Velmara dispense in a US specialty pharmacy or hub dispensing feed, grouped by initiation window. Window A is first fills in launch months 1-2 (3-month cut). Window B is first fills in launch months 1-3 (6-month cut). The final cohort is first fills in launch months 1-6. Initiators are defined as having no Velmara fill before the index fill. A Velmara dispense is assumed to imply the indicated population, because dispensing feeds often lack diagnosis. This assumption cannot be validated within the feed. It is tested only where diagnosis is recorded (for example hub enrolment forms), and the share of patients with a recorded diagnosis is reported. Age 65+ is reported only where age is available.","comparator":"None — descriptive; published osimertinib persistence is used only as an informal external reference and is not a formal comparison","outcomes":"3-month cut (window A, at least 3 months of potential follow-up): proportion with continued fills at 3 months using a 30-day permissible gap, and time to first missed refill (Kaplan-Meier with censoring at data-feed end), plus refill intervals. 6-month cut (window B, at least 6 months of potential follow-up): proportion persistent at 6 months using a 60-day permissible gap, matching TAC-008, with a 45-day sensitivity analysis, plus discontinuation and median time to discontinuation. Each estimate reports the number at risk at 1, 3 and 6 months. Estimates are flagged as unstable if fewer than 100 initiators are at risk. Coverage and leakage: estimated share of Velmara dispensing captured by the feed, and persistence under leakage-adjusted scenarios. Alignment: aggregate-level comparison of 6-month persistence with the TAC-008 estimate once available. Share of patients with a recorded diagnosis.","data_source":"A US specialty pharmacy or hub dispensing feed under a data-sharing agreement. No partner is identified or confirmed. The shortlist of partner types to approach before launch is (a) a commercial specialty pharmacy dispensing aggregator, (b) a national specialty pharmacy network or the largest specialty pharmacies directly, and (c) the manufacturer's own hub or patient-services vendor. Go/no-go: proceed only if the feed is estimated to capture at least 60% of Velmara dispensing, assessed by reconciling feed units against shipped or sold units within 8 weeks of launch. Fallback if coverage is below 60% or no agreement is reached by launch: report only the hub-enrolled cohort, labelled as selected and non-representative, or stop the bridge and rely on TAC-008. Aggregate-level alignment with TAC-008 is the default. Patient-level tokenised linkage is not assumed and would be added only if both data owners agree.","study_design":"Descriptive retrospective cohort of Velmara initiators identified from dispensing data, with the index date at first fill. Each cut uses a defined initiator entry window so that all included patients have the full potential follow-up. The 3-month cut includes initiators from launch months 1-2, with data through launch+5 months and readout at about launch+7 months. The 6-month cut includes initiators from launch months 1-3, with data through launch+9 months and readout at about launch+11 months. A final cut includes initiators from launch months 1-6, with data through launch+12 months and readout at about launch+14 months. Persistence is estimated with Kaplan-Meier methods, with censoring at the end of the feed or loss of channel visibility. Minimum at-risk numbers are stated for every estimate. The 3-month cut uses the 30-day gap and time to first missed refill, because a 60-day gap is uninformative at 90 days. The 6-month cut uses the 60-day gap. A coverage analysis estimates feed capture from unit reconciliation. Leakage sensitivity analyses assume a range of channel-switch rates among apparent discontinuers. Results are reported by payer type and, where age is recorded, age 65+. Every output is labelled 'interim dispensing-based bridge, not claims-based persistence' and is routed to P&T only as a bridge alongside the TAC-008 timeline.","duration_months":12,"readout_lag_months":2,"timing_rationale":"Launch is targeted for 2027-H1. Duration is measured from launch to the last data cut used for the 6-month analysis plus the final cut at launch+12 months. The 3-month cut needs a 2-month entry window plus 3 months of follow-up, so data close at launch+5 months. The 6-month cut needs a 3-month entry window plus 6 months of follow-up, so data close at launch+9 months. The final cohort needs 6 months of entry plus 6 months of follow-up, so data close at launch+12 months. (1) Lock before unblinding: the addendum, the thresholds, the decision rule and the censoring rules are written from VEL-201 data, simulation and blinded pooled (not by-arm) trial data. An independent statistician runs all by-arm CNS analyses, and the sponsor study team stays blinded to by-arm CNS results until the final cut. Thresholds are put to payer/HTA scientific advice for confirmation and are not assumed agreed. (2) Adequacy thresholds for the velmaratinib arm. (a) iORR lower exact 95% bound ≥35% (about 50% observed with n≈70 gives a lower bound of about 38%). (b) DoR: if ≥25 events at the cut, median DoR lower 95% bound ≥6 months. (c) Maturity: ≥25 DoR events, or at the fixed date ≥80% of responders with ≥6 months of follow-up from first response. (d) Decision rule: gap treated as closed if a, b and c are met. The share starting new therapy is estimated from blinded pooled data before the amendment is submitted. (5) Bayesian posterior probability that median DoR exceeds a pre-set clinically meaningful threshold, as sensitivity only. (6) Optional supportive precision-gain table using TAC-024 pooled output, only if available. The access checkpoint should be moved earlier, to about 31 July, so the 3-month build still delivers the interim table."},{"id":"GAP-001:proposal:2","verdict":"accept","rank":2,"confidence":65,"reason":"This is a cheap, transparent fallback and benchmark for the claims study, and the only route to EU5 tariff inputs. Its evidence is modelled and many frequency inputs will grade C or D. It earns a place as the second-ranked, de-risking tactic, not as the primary answer."}]},{"gap_id":"GAP-020","decisions":[{"id":"GAP-020:proposal:1","verdict":"accept","rank":1,"confidence":68,"reason":"This is a low-cost expansion of TAC-010 that adds BICR, extended MRI follow-up and pre-locked adequacy thresholds, and it directly tests whether the existing sub-study is adequate. The critic's data-cut defect is already fixed: the cut is now event-driven with a fixed-date fallback and landmark-based maturity criteria. It adds no patients and cannot meet the 2027 decision dates, but it is the sensible first step and the gate for any further cohort."},{"id":"GAP-020:proposal:2","verdict":"reject","rank":null,"confidence":30,"reason":"The cohort is expensive, needs about 50 sites, and reads out about 37 months after start. That is too late for the P&T and HTA filings it would support. Stand-alone it adds little precision over the existing sub-study. It is a contingent option that should be revisited only if the early gate from proposal 1 triggers it, so it should not be put to the evidence team now."}]}]}

calls.reply: {"gaps":[{"gap_id":"GAP-021","decisions":[{"id":"GAP-021:proposal:1","verdict":"accept","rank":1,"confidence":78,"reason":"Credible, validated active-comparator claims expansion of TAC-008 that answers the P&T ask directly. Persistence is limited to oral products and chemotherapy is reported separately. It reuses the parent's claims infrastructure at moderate incremental cost. It is honest that nothing on Velmara persistence can inform the 2027-03-31 decision."},{"id":"GAP-021:proposal:2","verdict":"accept","rank":2,"confidence":55,"reason":"The revision fixes the entry-window flaw the critic raised and gives a faster interim readout (about launch+7 and +11 months) than claims. It is clearly labelled a bridge and not the claims answer. Partner and coverage risk is managed by the 60% go/no-go and the fallback. It is lower quality and adds modest cost, so it ranks second as a supplement to TAC-008."}]},{"gap_id":"GAP-023","decisions":[{"id":"GAP-023:proposal:1","verdict":"accept","rank":1,"confidence":68,"reason":"Staged target trial emulation with trial IPD and US/EU5 real-world comparators. It has mortality linkage, a death-capture threshold, pooling and heterogeneity checks and a go/no-go, making it the strongest option for the adjusted elderly comparison. It is precision-based, not powered, and will miss the Jan/Mar 2027 dates. The NX-441 exclusion and index-year control should be tightened."},{"id":"GAP-023:proposal:2","verdict":"accept","rank":2,"confidence":52,"reason":"The revision adds registry-verified vital status and a 6-month landmark/RMST primary estimand, with hazard ratios exploratory, which resolves the critic's objections. It is a cheaper EU5 complement that reuses the chart review network, but it has no US component, wide precision and a small sample. It is acceptable as a secondary option beside proposal 1."}]}]}
